# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-11 22:54 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 294 active entries of tips_notebook.json (58 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, a group result whose other members are confirmed, or a switched claim. A role-block fully explains a missing result. But if one more kill would let the Yakuza block every nomination, it usually pays to hang the best case today. (seen in 44 games)
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of each player's stated vote on every nomination and trial, the announced totals and your own vote. More Guilty votes than stated Guilty usually means someone hid a vote, so quote the notepad when stories shift. (seen in 11 games)
- Totals can be altered on purpose: a Ballot Stuffer's trial vote counts twice, and a Fixer secretly flips one player's trial votes. When totals don't fit, first have everyone recheck their private reminder, since misposts are the commonest cause. Nomination Yes counts can't be altered, so they are the cleanest test for a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- Tokens die with you. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can swing a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die that night, so spend it a night early. (seen in 8 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. Still, a corroborated lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is close to proof, especially if they first denied the visit. (seen in 34 games)
- Keep tonight's plan in your will and post results publicly by day. A result from the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 32 games)
- Keep your votes matched to your stated reads and explain any switch beforehand. Answer questions about your night action plainly the first time, because evasion tends to become its own case. (seen in 32 games)

## Village
- Post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. Results held back tend to look retrofitted. (seen in 23 games)
- Once a player is shown Yakuza by a mechanical result, look next at who defended them, urged delay or PM'd them. Check those players' stated votes against the totals. (seen in 35 games)
- Keep tonight's target secret, in public and in PMs, and assume a hidden Wiretap reads every PM. A PM link is a lead to check, usually not grounds for a hang. (seen in 30 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers on purpose. A Serial Killer cause of death or a multi-death ignite proves one is alive, so keep a list of unwatched Vanilla claimants and unexplained survivors. While the Katana is still killing, avoid spending hangs on Neutrals that never block your win (Jester, Executioner, Bounty Hunter, Magpie). (seen in 3 games)
- Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged. Eager self-nominators and easily disproved lone claims are often Jesters. If you must hang one, aim for a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent, since the revenge hits a random Guilty voter. (seen in 16 games)
- On Day 2, avoid hinting at protective roles or tokens. While a Ritualist may be alive, don't name other players' exact roles in public. (seen in 24 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate, because the totals expose hidden defensive votes. Do the vote math in night chat. If your votes can't save them, vote Guilty and state the vote you actually cast. (seen in 45 games)
- Avoid daytime PMs to teammates, above all on Day 2 or when one of you is under pressure. Plan in night chat. (seen in 39 games)
- Before Day 2, agree a Village claim for each member that matches their tokens and real visits. Avoid Unique roles and anything Yakuza-only. Switching claims after one breaks usually hangs you faster. (seen in 23 games)
- Every member should submit the agreed holder and target every night. With two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 26 games)
- Don't flatly deny a visit that a watch, track or count could expose. Admit it with a cover prepared in night chat, and move the Katana once the holder is narrowed down. (seen in 17 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Remove the protector rather than retrying the same target. (seen in 23 games)
- Use rigs, puppets and cleans early. Rig a Day when a non-teammate is the likely nominee, never your own. (seen in 22 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so add that caveat when you post a Not Evil. A Not Evil player still usually ranks below unchecked players as a suspect, unless only one Yakuza can remain. (seen in 20 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle a live question, such as a hanged suspect or one side of a claim duel, not undisputed Katana victims. Post night, target and role at once, and don't announce your next exam. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Use free Standard protection on vocal analysts and claimed investigators, and vary your targets. Once you claim Medic, spend a token on self-protection within a night or two. You never learn whether a save happened, so never claim one. (seen in 27 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused shots is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 3, such as a claim conflict or an Evil read on an unverifiable claim, and fire a Basic shot once it is met. (seen in 13 games)

## Smuggler
- Plan swaps in night chat rather than vetoing them. To beat the Medic, aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with your real target. To dodge a check, swap yourself with a Villager. Both swapped players are told, so have a cover for your visits. (seen in 2 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 living players are doused, or 2 if you're being questioned. Each extra night spent dousing gives the town time to hang you. (seen in 12 games)

rules:
=== PART 1: THE GAME ===

R1 (Overview and winning)
You are playing a Mafia-style game with around 10 players (depending on setup), each in a faction. An omniscient
moderator runs the game. The game alternates Night and Day phases, starting with Night 1: there is no Day 1, so
the first Day is Day 2 (players write their first will before Night 1).
- For most roles, you win iff your faction wins. A faction typically wins iff it has players alive at the end.
- The game ends as soon as all living players, ignoring roles that never block wins, belong to one faction. This is
  checked after every death; deaths that happen together at night are checked together.
- Some Neutral roles never block another faction's win (their role says so); their own wins don't depend on how
  the game ends.

R2 (Factions)
- Village (Good): the largest faction, but with weaker roles and less information.
- Yakuza (Evil): fewer players, stronger roles; they know each other and share a night chat.
- Neutral: each Neutral player is their own one-person faction, even if two players have the same Neutral role.
The list of roles in the game is not public. A role may appear more than once in a game, except these unique
roles, which appear at most once: Smuggler, Vulture.

R15 (Alignments)
Every player has one of three alignments: Good (Village), Evil (Yakuza) or Neutral. Some roles and effects change
how a player's alignment appears; see R19.

R18 (Terms)
- Living players: players who haven't died or left. Every count in these rules ("majority", "random player")
  means living players unless it says otherwise.
- Majority: strictly more than half; exactly half is not a majority.
- Action: anything a role does at night by choice or by its rules (investigating, shooting, blocking, ...).
- Visit: an action on another player counts as A visiting B, unless it is an Astral Visit (R6).
- Astral Visit: an action that is not a visit. Abilities that react to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Trapper,
  Fortune Teller) never see or react to it.
- Alignment check: a result that reports alignment (Sheriff, Seer). See R19 for what they see.
- Exact-role check: a result that reports or tests an exact role (Oracle, Diviner, Ritualist, Mortician, Coroner,
  Talent Agent, a Vigilante's kill).
- Token: a limited-use resource a role starts with. Spent tokens are gone; a role-blocked action spends none.

R11 (The circle)
Players sit in a circle. The dead (and players who leave) are removed from it.

=== PART 2: THE DAY ===

R4 (Day phase, chat, nominations and trials)
Chat:
- There is a public chat and private chats between exactly two players.
- Private messages are not secret: whenever A sends B a private message, everyone sees that A sent B a private
  message, but only A and B see its contents.
Nominations:
- Any player may publicly nominate someone, including themself. All chat stops at once.
- Everyone votes Yes/No at the same time; nobody sees another vote before casting their own. The nominator votes
  Yes by default. There are no abstentions: a player who doesn't vote counts as voting No. Votes are secret: once
  all votes are in, only the number of Yes votes is announced (the nominator is named), never who voted which way.
  Each voter is privately reminded of their own vote.
- If a majority of all votes counted are Yes, the nominee goes on trial.
Trials:
- The nominee says the first public message and may defend themself; others may chat publicly and privately.
  After everyone else has had a turn, the nominee gets one last public message before the vote.
- Then everyone votes Guilty/Innocent at the same time (no abstentions: a player who doesn't vote counts as voting
  Innocent). Votes are secret: only the Guilty and Innocent totals are announced, never who voted which way. Each
  voter is privately reminded of their own vote.
- If a majority of all votes counted are Guilty, the nominee is Executed by Hanging, a Divine Attack, and the Day
  ends immediately.
- If three nominations pass (failed ones don't count) and all three trials end Innocent, the Day ends.
- Some roles can change how votes are counted. If an announced vote total doesn't match the number of voters,
  a role manipulated the count on purpose; it is not an error. One use of such a role can change every trial
  that Day, so the number of changed totals doesn't show how many times a role was used.
Voting Yes or Guilty on yourself is allowed.

R16 (Day length)
Day chat goes around the circle in turns. Each Day the program picks a random living player to speak first;
turns then go around the circle from them in the same order every round. Besides the endings in R4, the Day ends when a full round passes in
which nobody sends a public message or nominates, except that anyone sent a private message during that round
first gets one last turn. The Day also ends after at most 8 rounds.

R22 (Speaking budget)
Day messages and nominations cost speaking budget. Each player earns budget every round of a Day, up to a cap,
and part of what they have left carries into the next Day. A message's price grows with its length and, after
the first rounds of a Day, with the round; private messages cost less than public ones. A nomination costs
budget too. On a trial turn prices are lower and each speaker also gets a trial-only budget, spent first and lost
when the turn ends; the accused's first defense message is free up to a set length. The program sets the
numbers for each game and tells every player at the start.

R23 (Swaps)
Some roles can swap two players for a night. Every action that night aimed at one of them (including the Katana's
attack and automatic actions such as the Ex-Con's visit or the Seer's pair) lands on the other instead, as if its
user had chosen that player. Only the swap itself is not moved (the swapping player's Katana vote is). Results name the player the action's
user chose, so a swapped action's result doesn't show the swap: a Sheriff who checked A learns B's alignment as
A's. A result that lists several players (e.g. a group around the target) is built around B, but A and B trade
places in the list, each named where the other would be; the roles, alignments and counts in it are still the real
players', so the rest of the group can still hint at the swap. A Lookout who watched A watches B instead, and a
Tracker sees the player its target's action landed on. An effect that lasts into the next Day (e.g. listening in
on private messages) follows B, and its user is told at dawn that a swap moved it to B.

R13 (Last wills)
Players may write and update a last will before Night 1, at the beginning of each Day (except those who died the
night before) and during any of their own Day turns. When a player dies, their last will is shared publicly at once.

=== PART 3: THE NIGHT ===

R5 (Night phase)
Chat is off for most players; some (usually a faction, like the Yakuza) have a private night chat. The moderator
wakes players one by one, or faction by faction, to act. When the Night ends, the moderator works out every
effect. By default, effects are announced publicly at the start of the next Day; some are not announced.

R7 (Optional actions)
Every ability is optional ("may") unless its role says "must": any player may choose not to act at Night, not to
use a Day ability, and not to spend a token. Effects a role has automatically, with no choice (e.g. the
Ex-Con's nightly visit), aren't optional, but a role-block still stops them (R9).

R6 (Visits)
- When A performs an action on B, A visits B, unless the action is an Astral Visit.
- A role that targets a player may target itself unless its text says otherwise (e.g. "other than yourself").
- A player whose role can target others but who targets themself shows as visiting themself.
- A player whose action can only affect themself does not show as visiting anyone.
- An action that targets no player (e.g. the Clerk's rig) is not a visit.
- A player who visits the same target with several actions in one night is one visitor to that target: anything
  that lists, counts or reacts to visitors (a watch, a Veteran's alert, a trap) treats them once.

R9 (Role-blocks)
A role-blocked player's actions that night have no effect, exactly as if they had chosen not to act: no visit,
no tokens spent. It lasts only that one night (not the next Day or later nights). Role-blocked players are told
they were role-blocked. Any player can be role-blocked unless their role says otherwise; blocking a player who
has no night action, or who chose not to act, has no other effect, but they are still told. A role-blocker learns
only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked.
A result a role gets with no action at all (its text says "This needs no action") isn't an action, so a role-block
doesn't stop it; automatic actions, such as the Ex-Con's visit or the Seer's random pair, are stopped (R7).

R10 (Simultaneous night resolution)
All night actions happen at the same time. Think of it as two steps: first everyone attempts their actions,
then all results happen together. So investigations that give their result at the end of the night (e.g. the
Seer's random pair) draw from and report on everyone alive when the night began, including players who die that
night.

R21 (Effects that outlast their user)
An effect set up at night for the following Day (e.g. a Clerk's rig, a Prosecutor's prosecution) still happens if
its user dies that night, unless it needs its user to act during that Day (e.g. a Puppeteer writing the puppet's
messages, a Ballot Stuffer's doubled vote); those lapse. Any token spent on it is gone either way (R18).

R20 (Night resolution checklist): a summary of the rules above, in the order the moderator applies them.
1. Remove actions of role-blocked players (R9), automatic ones included (the Ex-Con's visit, the Seer's pair).
   Party Animal, Pharmacist, Smuggler and Veteran can't be role-blocked. Swaps (R23) apply before anything else.
2. Work out who visits whom (R6), including the Katana holder's visit (R8) and the Ex-Con's random visit.
3. Attacks: each kills iff its level beats the target's Defense (R3). Defenses don't stack; the highest counts.
   Traps hit non-Village visitors (Trapper).
4. Results for investigators, using the visits and appearances (R19).
5. Notifications: attackers learn whether they succeeded, attacked players learn the attacking role (R3, with the
   Katana exception in R8), protectors learn nothing (R17), role-blocked players are told (R9), Yakuza learn each
   other's actions (R8).
6. Deaths are revealed at the start of the Day (R12); the win check runs on all of the night's deaths together (R1).

=== PART 4: ATTACKS, DEATH AND INFORMATION ===

R3 (Attack and Defense)
- Levels, lowest to highest: None, Basic, Standard, Strong, Divine. Players have Defense None by default.
- An Attack kills iff its level is strictly higher than the target's Defense.
- Defenses don't stack: a player with several sources of Defense has the highest of them.
- By default the attacker learns whether the Attack succeeded (not the target's Defense), and the target learns
  the role that attacked them (not the attacker's name or Attack level). A target hit by several Attacks in one
  night learns the role behind each, including those that failed. The Katana is an exception (R8).

R17 (Protection feedback)
Protectors (e.g. the Medic) are never told whether their protection stopped an attack, and a protected player is
never told who protected them. A player who is attacked is still told as in R3.

R12 (Death reveals)
When someone dies, their cause of death (e.g. Katana, Vigilante, Execution by Hanging) and last will are revealed
publicly; their role and alignment are not. If several attacks were each fatal, every fatal cause is revealed;
attacks the player survived aren't. The dead leave the circle and can't take part in the game any more. A player
whose win ends their part in the game (a hanged Jester, an Executioner who leaves) is the exception: the
announcement of their win names their role.

R14 (Stall rule)
If a Day begins and nobody has died in the three previous Nights and three previous Days, everyone loses. Deaths
from last Night count even though they're announced today. Every death counts; leaving (like the Executioner's)
doesn't.

R19 (What investigations see)
Alignment checks (Sheriff: Evil / Not Evil; Seer: compares Good / Neutral / Evil) see a player's true alignment,
except:
- Yakuza holding the Katana at the end of the night: Good (Sheriff: Not Evil), even if they died that night.
- Player framed by the Fabricator that night: Evil.
- Ex-Con: Evil.
- Sheriff on Neutrals: Jester and Executioner read Evil; Serial Killer and Arsonist read Not Evil. (Seers see
  every Neutral as Neutral.)
The Census Taker's count is not an alignment check: it always sees true alignment, so none of the exceptions
above apply to it.
Exact-role checks see the true role. The Roleplayer is seen as "Roleplayer".
Token counts (Accountant) see the true total at the end of the night. The Roleplayer is seen as having 0 tokens,
even though they believe they have their fake role's tokens.
Visit-based results (Tracker, Lookout, Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Scout) are never changed by any of these.

=== PART 5: THE YAKUZA ===

R8 (Yakuza and the Katana)
- One random Yakuza starts with the Katana. The Yakuza share a private chat at night.
- Each night the Yakuza vote, at the same time, on who holds the Katana that night (and the next Day) and whom it
  attacks, if anyone. Both choices need a majority of living Yakuza; with two Yakuza alive, both must agree.
  Without a majority on a target, no attack happens; without a majority on a holder, the Katana doesn't move.
  A majority may move the Katana without attacking.
- The Katana attack is Standard and is dealt by whoever holds it at the end of the night. It is an action and a
  visit by that player (the new holder, if it moved that night): role-blocking them stops it, and Trackers see
  them visit the target. Moving or passing the Katana isn't an action: a role-block doesn't stop it (a blocked
  new holder still gets the Katana, but their attack fails), and it isn't a visit.
- The holder may also use their own role's night action.
- The holder appears Good to alignment checks that night (R19).
- The attacked player only learns they were attacked with the Katana, not the Yakuza role.
- At the end of the night, each Yakuza learns what actions the other Yakuza chose, but not their results
  (e.g. whether the Pharmacist's block worked) or whether a teammate was role-blocked.
- Role-blocked Yakuza still vote on the Katana's holder and target; the votes aren't actions.
- If the holder dies, the Katana passes to a random living Yakuza, if any; a holder who dies at night passes it on
  after that night's results. The living Yakuza are told who holds it now (and so learn that the holder died).

=== PART 6: ROLES ===

Every role lists the same fields. Defaults, unless a role says otherwise: Defense None, no tokens, appears as its
true alignment (R19), night action is a visit.

--- Village (Good) ---

Townsfolk (most villagers, helpful to the Village)

Vanilla Villager
  Night: none.

Investigative

Sheriff
  Night: may investigate one player. Learn Evil or Not Evil (alignment check, R19).

Tracker
  Night: may track one player. Learn whom they visited.

Lookout
  Night: may watch one player. Learn who visited them, not counting your own visit.

Seer
  Tokens: 1 seer token.
  Night: at the end of every night, you are told two random players other than yourself who were alive when the
  night began (players who die that night count, R10), and whether their alignments (Good/Neutral/Evil) are the
  same (alignment check, R19). Instead, you may spend a token to choose the
  two living players yourself (not including yourself). A chosen pair is a visit to both players; the random
  pair isn't a visit. A role-block stops both.

Fortune Teller
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn two numbers about that night, each labeled: how many players were
  visited (a player visited several times counts once), and how many players visited anyone (a player who visited
  several players counts once). This needs no action. Self-visits (R6) count in both numbers.
  Example: A holds the Katana, attacks B and also uses their own role's action on C, D visits B, and E protects
  themself. Visited: B, C and E, so 3. Visitors: A, D and E, so 3. Equal numbers don't mean nobody was visited
  twice.

Oracle
  Night: may guess one player's exact role (Astral Visit). At the end of the night, learn whether you were right.

Eavesdropper
  Night: may eavesdrop on one player. Only during the following Day (not the Night you eavesdrop), you read the contents of every private
  message they send or receive, as it is sent. Puppeted messages reach you as the puppet's (you aren't told about
  the puppeting). They aren't told.

Archivist
  Tokens: 1 archive token.
  Night: may spend the token to consult the archive. At the end of the night, let N be the number of players other
  than you who were alive when the night began (players who died that night count): you are shown N roles, in
  random order and without names, of which floor(0.5 * N) are real and the rest are fake. The real ones are the
  roles of floor(0.5 * N) of those players, chosen at random; a role appears as many times as it was drawn, so
  two drawn Vanilla Villagers show twice. This is an exact-role check (R19).
  Each fake is drawn at random from all the roles in these rules, including roles that are in the game, except
  that the result never shows a unique role (R2) twice.

Surveyor
  Tokens: 3 survey tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to survey one player other than yourself. The group is that player plus their nearest
  neighbor on each side in the circle (R11) among the players alive at the start of the night, skipping yourself
  and never counting anyone twice (so with only one or two other players alive, the group is smaller). You are
  told who was in the group and the exact role of one of them chosen at random, but not whose it is. Players who
  die that night can still be chosen. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Census Taker
  Night: may take a census around one player other than yourself (a visit to that player only).
  The program adds two other players drawn at random from everyone alive at the start of the night except you
  (players who die that night can be drawn; if fewer than two others are left, the group is smaller). It also
  draws at random whether to count Good or Evil players. You are told who was in the group, which alignment was
  counted, and how many of the group are of it. It counts true alignment and is not an alignment check (R19):
  the Katana holder, framed players and the Ex-Con count as what they really are, and
  Outsiders (e.g. the Roleplayer and the Ex-Con) count as Good. Neutral players are never
  counted, as either Good or Evil.

Coroner
  Tokens: 3 coroner tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to examine one player who died before the night began (not one who left the game, and not
  one who dies tonight). You learn their role, unless a Mortician cleaned them: then you learn only that. This is an
  Astral Visit (R6) and an exact-role check (R19).

Chronicler
  Tokens: 2 chronicler tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to mark one player other than yourself. This is a visit. The marked player isn't told.
  The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after you die. If a marked player dies, at any time and of any
  cause, the announcement of their death also reveals their true role to everyone (an exact-role check, R19), and
  says they had been marked by a Chronicler (not by whom). A Mortician's clean beats the mark: a marked player who
  is cleaned has their role and will hidden, and the announcement says they had been marked but the clean hid their
  role. You can't mark a player you already marked. Marking a player another Chronicler already marked spends your
  token but adds nothing.

Auditor
  Night: may audit one player other than yourself. You learn every vote they cast during the Day just before this
  Night, in order: Yes or No on each nomination and Guilty or Innocent in each trial. If they cast none, you learn
  that. A doubled vote (Ballot Stuffer) shows as a single Guilty or Innocent.

Juror
  Night: may name two different players other than yourself (dead players allowed; Astral Visit). You learn how many
  times they voted the same way, over every Day so far, counted separately for trial votes (Guilty/Innocent) and
  nomination votes (Yes/No), e.g. "the same way in 3 of 4 trial votes and 5 of 9 nomination votes". Only votes
  both of them cast count, and not votes on the nomination or trial of either of them. A doubled vote (Ballot
  Stuffer) counts once. You learn only the totals, not which votes they agreed on.

Bloodhound
  Tokens: 2 scent tokens.
  Night: at the end of every night, code draws three random players other than you from those alive at the start of
  the night, and you learn their names and how many Attacks (R3) they have made in total this game, tonight's
  included, whether or not the Attacks killed anyone. Each player's Katana attacks, shots, alert or trap hits and
  so on all count; a role-blocked attack never happened, so it doesn't. This needs no action and a role-block
  doesn't stop it.
  Night: may also spend a token to track one player other than yourself: they take one of the three places that
  night and code draws the other two. A role-block stops the tracking (R9) but not the result.

Scrutineer
  Night: may scrutinize one player other than yourself who voted in the Day's trials (Astral Visit). Code adds two
  random other players who voted in those trials (never you), and you learn the three names and, for each trial of
  the Day just before this Night, how many of the three voted Guilty, e.g. "2 in the trial of Erin; 0 in the trial
  of Frank". You don't learn which of them voted which way. A doubled vote (Ballot Stuffer) counts once. If there
  was no trial that Day, you learn that.

Profiler
  Tokens: 3 profile tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to profile one player other than yourself. You learn three different roles, exactly one
  of which is that player's true role. Of the other two, one is drawn at random from the roles of the other players
  alive at the start of the night (including players who die that night, but not yourself), and the other from the
  roles that no player in the game has. At least one of the three is a Good role and at least one is not Good (Evil
  or Neutral), so a result never settles the player's alignment on its own; which of the two supplies the missing
  side is random. When no role fits a draw, that one is drawn from all roles in these rules instead. The three are
  different and listed in alphabetical order. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Cartographer
  Tokens: 2 map tokens.
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn the sizes of that night's visit groups. Link two players whenever one
  visited the other that night (R6). Direction is ignored: A visiting B links them exactly as B visiting A
  would. A group is a set of players linked to each other, directly or through other players. Every player alive at
  the start of the night (including players who die that night) is in exactly one group, so a player who visited no
  one and was visited by no one is a group of 1, and a self-visit links no one. You learn only the sizes, largest
  first (e.g. "4, 2, 1, 1, 1"). This needs no action and a role-block doesn't stop it.
  Night: may also spend a token to map one player (Astral Visit; yourself allowed): at the end of the night you also
  learn the names of everyone in that player's group. A role-block stops the map (R9) but not the sizes.
  Your own actions never visit anyone, so they never link you to anyone.

Scout
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn the names of three players (you may be one of them) who were each in a
  different visit group that night. Groups are as for the Cartographer (visit direction is ignored). The names are
  drawn like this: a random player, then a random player outside the groups already drawn from, and so on, so a big
  group is more likely to come up than a small one. If there were fewer than three groups, you learn one name per
  group and how many groups there were. This needs no action and a role-block doesn't stop it. You never visit
  anyone.

Insomniac
  Tokens: 2 insomniac tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to stay awake. At the end of the night, you learn the roles of up to 3 players who visited
  someone that night (R6; a visit to themselves counts), but not who they are: if more than 3 players visited, 3 of
  them are drawn at random. The roles are listed in alphabetical order, and a role shows twice if two of those
  players have it. If fewer than 3 players visited, you learn all of their roles, and if nobody visited, you learn
  that. Players who visited and then died that night count. Only visits count: an action that isn't a visit (e.g.
  an Astral Visit or a Veteran's alert) doesn't. Staying awake is not a visit. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Accountant
  Night: may audit one player. Learn how many tokens they have in total at the end of the night, after any they
  spent that night and any a Magpie stole (token count, R19). You learn only the total, not what kind of tokens
  they are.
  If their role changed at the end of this night, the role just before the change counts.

Combat

Medic
  Tokens: 2 medic tokens.
  Night: may protect one player other than yourself, giving them Standard Defense. Spend 1 token to give Strong
  Defense instead, and 1 token to protect yourself instead of another player; the two can be combined (so
  protecting yourself costs 1 token with Standard Defense and 2 with Strong).

Trapper
  Night: may place a trap on one player other than yourself and other than the player your trap is already on, or
  may remove your trap (removing it isn't a visit). You have one trap at a time; a new trap replaces the old one at
  once. Traps last even after you die. A trap is armed from the next night on: the first time a
  non-Village player visits the trapped player on a later night, the trap is used up and that visitor is dealt a
  Strong Attack. If several non-Village players visit that night, one of them, chosen at random, is hit. You learn
  that your trap went off, and nothing else (not who, nor whether it killed).

Vigilante
  Tokens: 3 vigilante tokens.
  Night: may shoot one player: 1 token for a Basic Attack, 2 for Standard, 3 for Strong. If your shot kills them,
  you also learn their role (exact-role check, R19).

Veteran
  Tokens: 3 alert tokens.
  You can't be role-blocked.
  Night: may spend a token to go on alert (not a visit, R6, so nothing that reacts to visits counts it). While on
  alert you have Standard Defense and you deal a Strong Attack to every player who visits you that night, whatever
  their faction (a role-blocker who visits you is attacked too), however many there are. Astral Visits aren't
  visits, so they aren't attacked. At the end of the night you learn whether anyone visited you and, if so, how
  many, and whether your attack on each of them succeeded, but nothing about who they were.

Misc

Prosecutor
  Tokens: 2 prosecutor tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to prosecute someone. At the start of the next Day, before anyone speaks, the moderator
  announces that someone is being prosecuted; this counts as a successful nomination and they go to trial. It
  counts toward the Day's three-nomination limit, an execution ends the Day as usual, and it can combine with a
  Clerk's rig. If the trial needs a "nominator", the moderator picks a random player.

Party Animal
  Immune to role-blocks.
  Night: may visit one player, role-blocking them.

Philanthropist
  Tokens: 2 philanthropy tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to hand another player one token of their own role's kind (e.g. a medic token to a
  Medic; one kind chosen at random if their role has several). They are told a Philanthropist handed them a token.
  If their role has no tokens, they are told they threw it away because they have no use for it, so it doesn't
  count toward their tokens (e.g. for the Accountant). You are not told which happened.

Outsiders (Village roles: Good, and win with the Village, but the role helps the Village less or can hurt it)

Roleplayer
  You are told your role is X, chosen at random at the start from Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller,
  Oracle and Accountant.
  You aren't told that you're a Roleplayer. The moderator gives you results that are usually false but plausible.
  Exact-role checks see you as Roleplayer (R19). Your night actions only happen in your imagination: they aren't
  visits, have no effect, and no other role sees them.

Ex-Con
  Appears: Evil to alignment checks (R19).
  Night: every night you visit a random player other than yourself, and you aren't told whom. A role-block stops
  the visit (R7).

Cardinal
  If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the night you
  died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks, so the
  victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night.

--- Yakuza (Evil) ---
All Yakuza share the Katana and night chat (R8).

Grunt
  Night: none of its own.

Pharmacist
  Immune to role-blocks.
  Night: may role-block one player.

Ritualist
  Tokens: 2 ritual tokens.
  Night: may guess one player's exact role (Astral Visit), spending 1 token for a Standard Attack or 2 for a
  Divine Attack. If right, the Attack is dealt. If wrong, the moderator publicly announces at the start of the
  next Day that you are a Ritualist.

Puppeteer
  Tokens: 1 puppet token.
  Night: may spend a token to puppet any player for the following Day (puppeting yourself changes nothing). That
  Day, they are told they are being puppeted, and they can't chat or see private messages; nobody else is told. You
  chat publicly and privately in their place (including seeing their private messages) and can set their claim,
  which appears in the ledger as theirs; that is all you can do for them. They still nominate, vote and so on as
  normal. It lasts one Day.

Fabricator
  Tokens: 1 fabricator token.
  Night: may visit one non-Yakuza player to frame them (no token needed): that night they appear Evil to
  alignment checks (R19); other results are unchanged. On the same visit, you may spend a token to forge that
  player's last will (not anyone else's): if they die of any cause that night, your forged will replaces theirs.
  Framing and forging together are one visit.

Clerk
  Tokens: 1 clerk token.
  Night: may spend a token to rig the next Day's votes. On a rigged Day, anyone successfully nominated is executed.
  The Guilty/Innocent vote still happens; if a majority votes Guilty, the rig is not announced, otherwise it is
  announced publicly.

Smuggler
  Immune to role-blocks.
  Tokens: 2 swap tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to swap two different living players (yourself included) for the night (R23). You visit
  both of them. Both swapped players are told they were swapped, but not with whom.

Ballot Stuffer
  Tokens: 2 ballot tokens.
  Night: may spend a token so that during the following Day your vote counts twice in every Guilty/Innocent trial
  vote. It does not count twice in nomination (Yes/No) votes, which stay one vote each. A trial that Day needs a
  majority of all votes counted, so your extra vote counts whether you vote Guilty or Innocent. The announced
  totals include your extra vote without saying whose it is.

Fixer
  Tokens: 2 fixer tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to fix one player other than yourself. During the following Day, every Guilty/Innocent
  trial vote they cast counts as the opposite (Guilty as Innocent, Innocent as Guilty). Their nomination (Yes/No)
  votes are unchanged. Nobody is told, not even them: their private reminder shows the vote they cast, while the
  totals and anything that reports how they voted (e.g. the Auditor, the Informant, a Jester's revenge on Guilty
  voters) use the vote as counted.

Diviner
  Night: may pick one player. If they are Yakuza, they get Strong Defense for that night. Otherwise, the group is
  that player plus their nearest neighbor on each side in the circle (R11) among the players alive at the start of
  the night, skipping yourself and never counting anyone twice. You are told who was in the group and the exact
  role of one of them (exact-role check, R19), but not whose it is: it is the player you picked with 60% chance,
  otherwise one of the others (20% each, or 40% if there is only one other). Yakuza in the group and players who
  die that night can be drawn too.

Mortician
  Tokens: 3 mortician tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to try to clean someone. If they die that night by any cause, they are cleaned: their
  death is revealed publicly with its cause, but their last will shows as "cleaned by mortician". You are
  privately told their role and last will. A Coroner who examines a cleaned player learns nothing, and a
  cleaned player's role stays hidden even if a Chronicler marked them (the announcement says so). The token is
  spent even if they survive.

Wiretap
  You passively read the contents of every private message sent during the Day, between any two players. This is
  not a night action or a visit, so role-blocks don't stop it. Puppeted messages reach you as the puppet's (you
  aren't told about the puppeting). Nobody is told that a Wiretap exists.

Informant
  You passively see how every player voted in each Guilty/Innocent trial vote, right after the vote. This is not a
  night action or a visit, so role-blocks don't stop it. Nobody is told that an Informant exists, and the other
  Yakuza aren't told the votes: what you share in the night chat is up to you.

Talent Agent
  Tokens: 3 talent tokens, at most one a night.
  Night: may spend a token on one of these (not a visit; it targets no player). "In play" means the true role of a
  player alive when the night began (an exact-role check, R19):
  - Scan: learn one random non-Yakuza role that is in play and one random non-Yakuza role from these rules that
    isn't.
  - Count: name any role in these rules and learn how many players have it in play.

--- Neutral ---
Each Neutral player is their own faction (R2).

Serial Killer
  Defense: Standard. Appears: Not Evil to the Sheriff.
  Win: only alone (not even with another Serial Killer).
  Night: may deal a Strong Attack to one player.

Arsonist
  Defense: Standard. Appears: Not Evil to the Sheriff.
  Win: only alone (not even with another Arsonist).
  Night: may douse one player, or ignite (Astral Visit), dealing a Strong Attack to every doused player. A doused
  player who isn't Good (Yakuza or Neutral) is told at the end of the night that an Arsonist doused them; Good
  players are never told. Igniting uses up every douse: players who survive it are no longer doused.

Jester
  Defense: Basic. Appears: Evil to the Sheriff.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you are hanged during a Day (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if the game ends with you
  alive.
  Revenge: if you are hanged, the following night a random Guilty voter from your trial who was alive when that
  night began is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted Guilty, nothing happens.

Executioner
  Defense: Basic. Appears: Evil to the Sheriff.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  At the start you get a random target: any player except yourself.
  Win: iff your target is hanged during a Day while you are alive (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if
  the game ends with your target alive.
  On winning: the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game. Leaving works exactly like dying (you
  leave the circle for good) except it doesn't count as a death. The following night, a random Guilty voter from
  the trial who was alive when that night began (not you, since you left) is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted
  Guilty, nothing happens.
  If your target dies any other way, or leaves the game, you become a Jester.

Bounty Hunter
  Tokens: 1 attack token. Never blocks wins (R1).
  At the start you get 3 random targets: any players except yourself.
  Night: may spend the token to deal a Strong Attack to one player.
  A bounty on a target is claimed if they die by your attack or are hanged during a Day while your vote counted as
  Guilty. If a target dies any other way (or leaves the game), that bounty is lost. Night deaths are simultaneous
  (R10): a target you kill on the night you die still counts.
  Win: iff you claim 2 bounties. If you are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game
  (leaving works as for the Executioner). If you have died, you still win and nothing is revealed.
  Lose: once you can no longer claim 2 bounties; if you are alive, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave
  the game.

Magpie
  Defense: Basic. Never blocks wins (R1). Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens.
  Night: may steal a token from another player (a visit). It happens at the end of the night, after that night's
  token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen. The stolen token is gone (you can't use it). You are told
  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told.
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and max(floor(N/4), 2) or fewer
  players are alive, counting yourself, where N is the number of players at the start of the game. The game then
  ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles that never block wins still count, R1).
  Night: none.
  Day: at the start of each Day, you learn a role for each player who died since the previous Day began (during that
  Day or the night after it; not players who left the game): with 50% chance it is their true
  role (exact-role check, R19), otherwise it is a different role drawn at random
  from all the roles in these rules. You aren't told which. This isn't an action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

reasoning:
Thinking about Dave's Bloodhound claim: his random draw of Grace, Ivan, and Olivia yielding zero attacks fits a truthful reading, and Bloodhound isn't on the Roleplayer list, though he could still be lying as a Neutral. A wrong Ritual guess would expose me, and Dave's claim felt detailed with the two scent tokens mentioned.

Bob's Cartographer count also seems plausible as genuine since guessing an exact match like two visits with eleven singles would be risky for a faker, which makes me suspect Grace and Heidi's claimed visits mean they're Roleplayers or liars rather than Bob being fake — though I can't fully verify since I only know Alice's visit to Niaj. The real danger is Dave: if he's a genuine Bloodhound and scents Alice tonight, her attack count would increase, which could expose her.

For killing Dave, I'm weighing a Divine ritual with two tokens for certainty against a Standard attack that a Medic could block. Since nobody's claimed Medic and Bob's count suggests no one protected on night one, a Medic blocking Dave seems unlikely, so spending the extra token on Divine feels justified given my roughly 85% confidence Dave truly is Bloodhound.

I think keeping the Katana with Alice makes sense—worst case she's still caught with one token, and spreading risk doesn't help since no real Lookout/Tracker claims exist. As for targeting Grace, killing her risks wasting a kill if she's just a harmless Roleplayer, especially if Bob's Cartographer count checks out and Grace/Heidi turn out to be Roleplayers or liars.

If Bob were a genuine village Cartographer, lying about the map wouldn't make sense unless he's baiting—so he's more likely Neutral, faking the role. Since no Executioner reveal happened for Heidi, that rules out Bob being an Executioner with her as target, pointing more toward Jester.

If Bob's claim is fabricated, that suggests Grace is likely the real Accountant and Heidi the real Lookout, which makes Grace someone to watch closely.

The stated votes line up fine, nothing suspicious there. I need to figure out what fake N2 guess to feed the team — something bland and wrong for my log, while deciding whether claiming a result like "guessed Bob = Cartographer, right" helps credibility without accidentally protecting Bob when we actually want him hanged Day 3.

If Bob's a village Cartographer, hanging him is good for us; if he's a Jester, hanging him wastes the village's day with only minor revenge risk, which also suits us since killing villagers is the priority. A fake guess saying "Bob = Cartographer: WRONG" would push hard to hang him, but it's risky if a Coroner later reveals he really was one — so I'm weighing that against something blander like an Oracle guess on Grace to indirectly support the push toward hanging Bob.

For now I'll keep the message safe: agree with the group and confirm the ritual pairing of Dave as the Bloodhound target, framing it as using one token.

I'm also weighing whether Dave could be a fake — his draw named three true non-holders, but that doesn't fully confirm him. If the ritual fails and he survives, he'd call out an attack and cast doubt on my Oracle claim; if he scented Alice, that's even worse for me. With two tokens I could guarantee the kill if the role guess is right, but spending both leaves me essentially powerless afterward, so I need to weigh that cost carefully.

The upside of landing an extra kill in the same night is big — effectively two kills in one turn. Medic odds still seem low given the single N1 visit, so I'm leaning toward committing just one token. Carol as a later Juror ritual target and Mallory as Philanthropist are other options to keep in mind, and I'll keep the Katana plan as is rather than redirecting it to Dave. Now I just need to draft a message under 200 words and decide whether to mark ready, though I might hold off until others weigh in on the log change.

reasoning:
Eight players remain, with Yakuza holding Alice, Frank, and Judy against five non-Yakuza: Carol, Erin, Ivan, Mallory, and Olivia. Bob, revealed as the Jester, gets his revenge tonight — a random Guilty voter from his trial will be struck by a Divine Attack, so I need to work out who voted Guilty.

Judy claimed she voted Innocent, meaning the seven other alive Guilty voters are Alice, Carol, Erin, Frank, Ivan, Mallory, and Olivia — giving Alice or Frank only a 2/7 chance of being hit versus 5/7 for a villager. Combined with tonight's Katana kill, if both strike villagers we'd drop to six players, three Yakuza against three others, which creates a problem: nominations require a majority of six, and Yakuza alone can't reach that threshold, so we'd need at least one villager vote to force a trial, after which my doubled ballot could secure a Guilty majority.

Reassessing claims, I realize Bob being the Jester invalidates his visit counts as fabricated rather than genuine Cartographer data, which actually makes Heidi and Grace's claims (Lookout and Accountant) more credible as real roles, and by extension supports Mallory's Philanthropist claim toward Dave as legitimate. Ivan's vague-then-copying behavior also fits a real Scrutineer pattern, since his stated results (Dave Guilty, Mallory Guilty, Grace Innocent) align plausibly with an early push for a trial.

Thinking through tonight's optimal play: Katana and Ritual kills plus a possible Jester revenge kill could drop villagers from 8 to 5, giving us 3 Yakuza against 2, enough to control nominations and finish them off — though I need to watch for the Jester's revenge hitting the same target as the Katana or even hitting me, though simultaneous resolution should mean my attack still lands and the Katana passes on regardless.

A wrong Ritual guess would publicly expose Judy, and she's already somewhat suspected as "Oracle." Carol's claim as Juror seems plausible given her stated results, though I can't rule out she's faking or is actually some neutral role like an Arsonist or Serial Killer — there's been no failed kill to confirm a Medic exists. For tonight I'm weighing Katana on Ivan, who's suspicious of me as the Scrutineer, against Ritual on Carol as the Juror with a Standard guess, keeping in mind a Medic protecting Carol could cause the Ritual to fail silently without exposing Judy.

I'm also considering alternatives: Katana on Carol with Ritual on Mallory (claimed Philanthropist, gave tokens to Dave) or Ivan (claimed Scrutineer but vaguely). The Jester's revenge pool includes Alice, Carol, Erin, Frank, Ivan, Mallory, and Olivia, so killing two from that list risks a roughly 2/7 chance the revenge boomerangs onto one of our own kills, a 2/7 chance it hits us directly, and a 3/7 chance it strikes another villager — which makes me wonder if a Smuggler-style swap from Frank could redirect that outcome.

Working through the swap math, I realize swapping a pool member with a non-pool player like Judy just shifts where the random revenge lands without any net benefit, and swapping two pool members (like Alice and Carol, or Frank and another villager) is symmetric — whichever one would've been hit just trades places, so there's no actual gain from rearranging who the Katana or revenge targets within the pool.

I'm mapping out D4 scenarios: if katana, ritual, and revenge all hit distinct villagers, we end up 3Y vs 2V and control the outcome entirely, so no token spend needed there. But if revenge instead strikes one of our own kill targets, the math shifts.

With 6 alive and a stuffer vote, nomination still needs 4 Yes and trial needs majority of the 7 votes counted, meaning 4 for majority. We'd have exactly 4 Guilty with the stuffer, but passing a nomination still requires at least one villager going along. If villagers nominate a fellow villager, we pile on; if they try to nominate one of us, they only have 3 votes against our 6, so we simply vote No and the nomination fails.

But if all three of us vote No together, that openly reveals us as a bloc, especially since it's already looking like a 3v3 split. For a villager nominee's trial, it'd be 3 Innocent votes from villagers against our 3 Guilty—a 3-3 tie with no majority, but the stuffer pushes it to 4-3 and hangs them, so that token is valuable tomorrow in this scenario. There's also a defensive angle if one of us ends up on trial once 6 remain. If revenge kills take out me or Frank, we'd drop to 5 alive with nomination needing 3, which villagers could reach—so I need to think through how dangerous that coordination risk is.

With the stuffer active while I'm alive, a trial among 6 voters needs 4 Guilty to hang, but villagers only have 3, so they can't convict us—my doubled Innocent vote pushes the total to 6, keeping majority at 4 and protecting us. Offensively though, nominating a villager needs 3 Yes votes out of 5, and we only have 2, so that's a problem. Tokens die with me and lapse if I'm killed that night, so with only a couple days left in the game, I should spend one tonight and save the other for tomorrow—though the vote count mismatch would eventually expose the stuffer's existence, which may not matter much by then. I'm also weighing who should hold the Katana now: no Tracker or Lookout remains alive to expose me, Heidi's dead, and if Jester revenge kills me the attack still resolves simultaneously since no one's claimed Sheriff to call out the holder as suspicious.

Judy stands out as a good holder since she's not in the Jester revenge pool and her correct Innocent vote on the Jester now makes her look sharp and trustworthy to the village, even though some might wonder if she "knew" something. Turning to who to target next, I'm sizing up the remaining threats—Carol as the analytical Juror leader, Ivan who's suspicious of me and others, Mallory with her Philanthropist token, and the vanilla villagers Erin and Olivia who've both been quietly perceptive. For a Day 4 mislynch, I'm considering Ivan as a strong candidate since his Scrutineer claim conflicts with Frank's identical claim, creating a useful rivalry to exploit.

With Bob's Jester reveal, I'm reassessing the whole picture: Heidi now looks innocent, Grace's Accountant claim seems real, and suspicion needs redirecting away from the Yakuza's apparent choice to kill Grace specifically for her real info role. I'm also tracking how Carol's Juror vote comparisons and Judy's Oracle claim tied to the Ritualist's kill on Dave could bring new scrutiny onto Judy if I'm not careful.

For tonight's kill, I'm weighing Carol and Ivan as top targets since removing them collapses the remaining villager pool down to Erin, Mallory, and Olivia — people I can plausibly steer toward a lynch given Mallory and Olivia's weak defenses of Bob, while Erin stays town-read and dangerous. I'm also considering swapping Ivan for Erin and instead letting Frank's fake Scrutineer result clash with Ivan's real one, since Ivan's actual trio scrutiny from Day 3 could expose Judy if the numbers don't line up.

The real threat isn't Carol's Juror or Ivan's info role — it's pure vote math. I'm running the revenge-kill probabilities: if it lands outside tonight's kill/ritual targets, we're basically at 3-vs-2 and control the nominations; if it hits one of our kills, we drop to 3-vs-3 but can still force a split or survive the following night to end up favored, since villagers can't reach the four Yes votes needed to hang us at that ratio.

If the revenge hits Alice or Frank though, things get dicier — with only two of us left plus a dead stuffer or no stuffer, villagers inch closer to the numbers needed to hang, and if it hits me specifically, Frank and Judy are left facing three unified villagers, which is a much harder fight. So the ritual target really does matter a lot here.

Given that, I think the ritual should be used tonight — speed matters, though a wrong guess risks outing Judy, so I need to pick my most confident read. Carol reads strongly as a Juror to me, since that role isn't on the Roleplayer list and she doesn't fit a lying villager or neutral profile well. Ivan reads strongly as a Scrutineer too — his very first D2 message, pushing for a trial to get recorded votes before anyone had even claimed, is classic Scrutineer behavior and came before Frank's fake claim.

I'm also weighing where a hidden Medic might be sitting — likely tucked under one of the unclaimed vanillas, Erin or Olivia — and thinking through whether Frank's swap ability could let me beat a Medic's protection by aiming the Katana at a decoy, swapping that decoy with the real target, and landing the kill where it counts even if someone's being shielded.

But the swap reveals itself to both swapped players, which would tip off the Yakuza about the Smuggler role at little real cost, and I need to think through how a Jester's revenge interacts with the swap — whether it lands on the already-dying target (wasted) or gets redirected onto someone else entirely (a bonus kill).

With only two swap tokens left and the game nearing its end, I should use it. Frank visits both players, but that's not something Tracker or Lookout claims would expose since neither has surfaced alive. The real question is whether the Medic is more likely to protect Carol, the outspoken Juror, over Olivia, the quiet Vanilla — if so, the swap helps regardless of Medic's choice, and the ritual should target whichever of the two is least likely to be shielded.

So I'll aim Katana at Olivia as the decoy, swap her with Carol since Carol's the most probable protection target, and send the ritual at Ivan to confirm the Scrutineer. Swapping Olivia and Carol doesn't interfere with the ritual since that's targeting Ivan separately. I also want to make sure the decoy isn't someone the Medic would obviously protect — Olivia being the quietest player makes her a safer choice for that role.

Now I'm weighing which pair of kills leaves the best remaining villager lineup after Day 4 — comparing Carol+Ivan versus Carol+Erin as targets and what survivors each scenario leaves behind.

If Ivan, Mallory, and Olivia remain, Ivan would actually vote Yes against Mallory or Olivia since he already suspects them, which helps secure a villager Yes on a future nomination. Meanwhile Mallory and Olivia suspect Ivan too from the Day 2 push, so that trio dynamic could work in my favor.

This leaves Carol and Erin as the cleared town leaders worth targeting — Carol as Juror is a safer ritual claim than Erin's Vanilla role, though Medic protection odds complicate things since Carol seems more likely to be guarded.

I'm uncertain whether the Medic is even still alive—both nights' kills succeeded, so the odds of a Medic among the 5 remaining feel low, maybe 20-25%. Still, the swap costs little to attempt even if the payoff is uncertain.

Thinking through the actual combination: Katana targets Erin directly, while the ritual aims at Olivia as "Juror" with a swap between Olivia and Carol. Since Smuggler abilities can't be role-blocked, the swap should go through reliably—the real risk is just Frank submitting it correctly. If he botches it, the ritual lands on the wrong role and Judy gets outed, so the benefit only materializes if the Medic was actually protecting Carol.

Weighing this against alternatives: a direct ritual on Carol as Juror with Katana swapped from Olivia onto Erin would at least fail safely if the swap misfires, just killing Olivia instead of causing a catastrophe—though Erin now looks heavily town-credentialed after the Heidi vote, so Medic coverage there seems unlikely anyway. A third option targets Carol with the Katana/swap combo and puts the ritual on Ivan as Scrutineer instead, leaving Erin, Mallory, and Olivia as the remaining threads, with Erin's pointed questioning of Mallory, Ivan, and Olivia about their roles standing out as worth tracking.

Mostly I think we win through sheer numbers in most branches; the dangerous case is a revenge kill landing on me or Frank, which could flip the end state to 2 Yakuza vs 3 villagers—and in that scenario, Judy, having claimed Oracle and Ritualist while dodging revenge, becomes the obvious suspect for a coordinated villager lynch, while a divided trio of Ivan/Mallory/Olivia actually works in our favor compared to a unified one. Frank's position as Scrutineer also shifts depending on whether Ivan survives to split suspicion.

If Frank dies instead, my active stuffer token becomes critical since it blocks a majority hang even with Judy and me against three villagers, so protecting tonight's ballot matters a lot. My plan: ritual-guess Carol as Juror since she's the clearest vote-auditing target, send the Katana after Erin to remove the leading town-read voice, and consider a Frank swap to dodge a Medic—likely protecting Carol, Erin, or Judy/Ivan, with Carol as my best guess for who gets saved, meaning the ritual might fail without exposing Judy.

Trying to route the Katana through a swap onto Carol feels riskier since it'd require guessing the Medic's target correctly, and Erin's consistent vanilla claim could be masking a real power role, making that ritual guess too uncertain. I keep weighing these combinations but none clearly beats the straightforward option: ritual on Carol, Katana directly on Erin, saving the swap for contingency.

I can't predict a hypothetical Vigilante or SK targeting us anyway. I'll let teammates weigh in since this is round 1 of 3, then propose the plan concisely in under 200 words and note I'm spending a ballot token tonight.

For Day 4, I'm keeping the holder with me so revenge passes if I die, and planning for Judy to take credit for calling the Jester while we push Mallory or Ivan as targets, with a No vote if we're nominated in a 3v3. I should also give Judy's fake N3 Oracle guess something bland, and watch out that if Carol dies to the Ritualist, suspicion on "Oracle" Judy increases unless our numbers dilute it. I also want to double-check the guilty count.

Something seems off — 8 Guilty and 1 Innocent suggests Judy voted Innocent, meaning Bob voted Guilty on himself. I should ask Judy to confirm she voted Innocent so she's excluded from the revenge pool, then draft the message and set ready=false while I wait for replies.

title: Post-game feedback: rules, interface and bugs (debrief)

task:
We're improving this game and the program that runs it. Out of character now, answer from your own experience of playing it. Be specific and concrete, and write 'none' where you have nothing to say.
- confusing_rules: Which rules, or parts of your instructions, were confusing or ambiguous?
- missing_information: What information did you need but not have, or find hard to keep track of?
- wanted_but_couldnt: What did you want to do that the game or interface didn't let you do?
- bugs_or_oddities: Did anything seem broken, inconsistent with the rules, or strange?
- suggestions: What would you change about the game or the interface?

output.confusing_rules:
1. Philanthropist: the rules don't say whether a gift can push a recipient above their starting token count, whether a token handed over tonight can be spent tonight, or whether the gift still lands if the recipient dies that night. Dave's log suggests it is added after his own spend, but I had to guess while playing.
2. Philanthropist and swaps (R23): my N3 gift to Erin was moved to Olivia and I was never told. That is by the rules, but for a role with no feedback at all it means my only proof (the recipient confirming) can silently point at the wrong person. The role text could note this.
3. Phase labels such as "[Day 2 night] Night 2 begins" are awkward. "Night 2" alone would be clearer.
4. R1's win check: on Day 4 the Yakuza were 3 of 4 living players and controlled every vote, yet the game ran on. That is correct by the rules, but a line saying there is no early "majority" win would help.
output.missing_information:
1. As Philanthropist I get no result line at all, not even "your token was delivered". I had to infer I wasn't role-blocked from the absence of a block notice.
2. There is no public or private indication of which claimed roles hold tokens, so choosing a recipient was guesswork from the rules text.
3. Bob's claim in the ledger ended in "[truncated]", which cut off his stated trial vote. That was the very thing being argued about on Day 3.
4. Stated votes against totals had to be tracked by hand in the notepad. A per-trial table of stated votes next to the announced totals in the ledger would save a lot of notepad space.
output.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. Prove my role. A Philanthropist can only be confirmed by a living, honest, token-holding recipient. I gave to Dave, who died the same night, and the Jester then used "unconfirmable by design" against me.
2. Ask a private follow-up during a trial without paying for it from the same small budget as the public statement I needed to make.
3. Keep a fuller vote log. The 425-word notepad was about 80% full by Day 3 of a 13-player game.
output.bugs_or_oddities:
1. The post-game "Night 3 actions" list is inconsistent with the other records. It shows my target as Olivia and Alice's Katana as attacking Erin (the landed targets), while my own night history says Erin and the Yakuza summary says Olivia (the chosen targets). Nothing marks which is which.
2. The ledger lists "Bob (role hidden, executed by hanging)" and on the next line "Bob (Jester) won". This is harmless but contradictory.
3. Four Village-side deaths in one night (Katana, Ritualist, Jester's revenge, Cardinal's curse) took the game from 8 alive to 4 with all 3 Yakuza untouched. The revenge hitting the Cardinal chained into a second Divine kill on a Good player, so one mis-hang cost three Villagers. This follows the rules but is extremely swingy.
4. The Day 4 total "4 Guilty, 1 Innocent of 4 voters" publicly exposed a Ballot Stuffer. It didn't matter here, but the stuffed vote was wasted on a trial the Yakuza already controlled.
output.suggestions:
1. Give the Philanthropist a minimal receipt each night ("your token was handed over", without saying whether it was useful), or tell them when a swap moved the gift.
2. In post-game logs, show both targets for swapped actions, e.g. "chose Erin, landed on Olivia (swap)".
3. Never truncate the vote part of a ledger claim. Truncate the free text first, or put votes in their own field.
4. Add an auto-maintained table of stated votes against totals to the ledger.
5. Consider stopping the Cardinal's curse from triggering off Jester's or Executioner's revenge, or capping non-Yakuza chain deaths per night, so one bad hang can't remove three Villagers.
6. With 13 players, a hand-picked setup of 3 strong Yakuza (Ritualist, Smuggler, Ballot Stuffer), a Jester, a Magpie and a Cardinal against a Village with no protective or killing role and mostly vote-reading investigators felt close to unwinnable. A Medic or one alignment-checking role would balance it.
7. Raise the notepad cap for games with 12 or more players.

output.confusing_rules:
1. R23 (swaps) versus automatic effects. It is unclear whether a Jester's revenge or a Cardinal's curse counts as an "action aimed at" a player and so gets moved by a swap. On Night 3 I was told "any action aimed at you landed on them instead", yet I died to Jester's revenge the same night. I could not tell whether the revenge drew Erin and was swapped onto me, or drew me and ignored the swap.
2. R23 versus notifications to the target. The rule says results name the player the user chose, but it does not say who receives target-side messages such as "a Philanthropist handed you a token" (see bugs).
3. Cardinal. The text does not say whether the curse can be stopped by any Defense (it is Divine, so presumably not), or whether the victim's death announcement always names "Cardinal's curse". It did, which publicly confirms that a Cardinal died and that the victim was Good. That is worth stating in the role text, because it decides whether the Cardinal should claim.
4. "Outsider" Cardinal gives no guidance on whether hiding the role is expected. I claimed Vanilla, and the fake claim then became part of other players' case against me.
output.missing_information:
1. No role is ever revealed on death, so with 13 players the Village never learned whether the Heidi hang was right. Every later day was built on an unresolved guess, and I had no result of my own to anchor on.
2. The setup range (2 to 4 Yakuza, 0 to 3 Neutrals) is wide. I could not do parity maths, such as "how many mislynches can we afford", with any confidence.
3. Keeping every player's stated vote for each nomination and trial in a 425-word notepad was tight by Day 3. I had to drop older detail to fit the vote log.
4. In the ledger, Bob's final claim was cut off with "[truncated]" exactly where his corrected vote statement was. That was the part that mattered.
output.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. I had no way to act on my role at all. Cardinal has no night action, no day ability and no information, so my whole game was chat plus votes. I would have liked some lever, even a one-time one, such as privately proving my role to one player.
2. I wanted to tell one trusted player I was the Cardinal without everyone seeing that a PM was sent and without a possible Wiretap reading it. The only safe channel was my will, which is only read after the damage is done.
3. I wanted to see my own vote history in the ledger automatically instead of logging it by hand in the notepad.
output.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Probable swap bug. On Night 3 Frank swapped Olivia and Erin, and Mallory (Philanthropist) targeted Olivia. By R23 the gift should have landed on Erin, but I (Olivia) received "A Philanthropist handed you a token, but you threw it away". Either the gift was not moved by the swap, or the notification went to the chosen target instead of the real recipient. Both of us were tokenless, so the effect was hidden, but with a token role it would matter.
2. In the same night I was told every action aimed at me landed on someone else, yet I was killed by Jester's revenge. That may be correct (revenge drawn on Erin, then swapped), but nothing in the log lets anyone verify it.
3. The end-of-game reveal is inconsistent. The Night 3 action list says "Katana vote: Alice holds, attacks Erin" for all three Yakuza, while their chat, the Yakuza summaries and Alice's result all say the target chosen was Olivia. The action list seems to show the post-swap target while the results show the chosen one.
4. This post-game questionnaire still showed me a live-style prompt (ledger, notepad, will and "every response has a reason field" instructions), although I had been dead since Night 3.
output.suggestions:
1. Make R23 explicit about which effects a swap moves: revenge, the Cardinal's curse, Philanthropist gifts and Magpie steals. Also say who gets the target-side notification.
2. Give the Cardinal some agency or information. As written it is a pure liability with nothing to do for the whole game. Alternatively, say plainly in the role text that the curse's cause of death is announced, so the player can weigh claiming.
3. Have the program add each player's own nomination and trial votes to their private history. That frees the notepad for reads.
4. Raise the notepad cap, or exempt an auto-generated vote table from it, in 13-player games.
5. Do not truncate claim text in the ledger mid-sentence. If it must be cut, drop the oldest claim history first.
6. Consider revealing the alignment (not the role) of hanged players, or including a guaranteed Coroner in larger hand-picked setups. In this game the Village hanged a Lookout, a Jester and a Scrutineer and never received one confirmed fact.
7. In the end-of-game log, show both the chosen target and the swapped landing target for each action.

output.confusing_rules:
1. The Roleplayer rule left me unable to trust my own role. Accountant is on the Roleplayer list, so I had to hedge every claim with "unless I'm a Roleplayer". The fake Cartographer (Bob, actually the Jester) used exactly that to wave away two real visitors, Heidi and me. The rules give no way for a listed role to ever confirm it is real, and it wasn't clear to me whether that is intended.
2. R6/R18 say the Accountant audit is a visit by default, but the Accountant entry doesn't say so itself. I had to infer it from "Defaults: night action is a visit". A "(a visit)" tag on each role's Night line, like the "(Astral Visit)" tag, would remove the doubt.
3. The Cartographer's text "Your own actions never visit anyone" was easy to misread on Day 2. It took me a while to be sure my audit of Heidi still should have shown up in Bob's count.
4. R23 swaps in the end-of-game log: the "Night 3 actions" list appears to show where actions landed (Alice "attacks Erin", Carol "second target Olivia"), while the private results name the chosen player ("attack on Olivia succeeded", "Judy and Erin"). Nothing says which convention the log uses.
output.missing_information:
1. My Night 2 result (Bob has 0 tokens) would have proved Bob was not a Cartographer, but it arrived with my death and could never reach my will. I knew this was the rule (R13), yet it meant my one decisive result was lost.
2. A per-role note on token counts would have helped. I built my own table in the notepad of how many tokens each role starts with, which ate about 80 of my 425 words.
3. I had no clean view of who had stated which vote. I tracked stated votes against totals by hand in the notepad. The ledger's Claims section holds them, but buried inside long free-text claims, and one was cut off as "[truncated]".
output.wanted_but_couldnt:

2. Check whether I was a real Accountant. I planned to audit a known token count as a self-test and did, but never got a Day to use it.
3. Speak more than once during Heidi's trial. I had one turn and couldn't reply to Bob's later "stall" argument before the vote.
output.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Bob's Day 3 claim shows as "[truncated]" both in the ledger and in the log line itself, so his final stated trial vote was cut off.

3. The Night 3 log has Alice's "Katana vote: attacks Erin" alongside "Your Katana attack on Olivia succeeded" and a summary saying she "chose to attack Olivia". This is presumably the swap, but it reads as a contradiction.

output.suggestions:
1. Balance: this hand-picked setup gave the Village no protector, no killer and no Sheriff, Tracker or Coroner, against 3 Yakuza (Ritualist, Smuggler, Ballot Stuffer) plus a Jester and a Magpie. The two visit-based Village investigators (Lookout, Accountant) were both on the Roleplayer list, so a Jester's fake Cartographer count discredited them at no cost. Either include at least one Roleplayer-proof confirming role, or drop the Roleplayer shadow when no Roleplayer is in the game.
2. Give the Claims ledger structured vote columns (nomination and trial vote per player per Day) instead of free text, and don't truncate claims.
3. Tag each role's Night line explicitly as "visit" or "Astral Visit".
4. Consider letting a dying player's final-night result be appended to the will, at least for roles with no other way to get it out. Otherwise say prominently in the role text that it will be lost.
5. Say in the post-game log whether action targets are shown as chosen or as landed when a swap happened.
6. Raise the notepad cap slightly or supply a built-in vote tracker. Most of my notepad went on bookkeeping the program already knows.

output.confusing_rules:
1. R23 swaps and Astral Visits: I didn't realise a swap also redirects an astral, non-visit check like the Juror's. On N3 I named Judy + Erin and was told "1 of 2 trial votes"; Judy's and Erin's real votes give 0 of 2. Only the end-of-game log (Frank swapped Olivia and Erin) showed I had actually been compared against Olivia. R23 does say "every action", but a short line in the Juror, Scrutineer and Oracle texts saying a swap can silently redirect them would help.
2. Juror exclusion clause ("not votes on the nomination or trial of either of them"): clear once read carefully, but the result never says how many votes were excluded. I had to work out the denominators by hand.
3. R1 win check: on Day 4 there were 3 Yakuza and 1 Villager alive and the game still ran a full Day. That follows the rules as written (no parity ending), but I only learned by watching that the Village needs every Yakuza dead and gets no early loss call.
4. Self-claiming under a Ritualist: the tips say to post your role in your first speech and also not to name others' exact roles while a Ritualist may be alive. Nothing covers the fact that your own public exact claim is just as much a Ritualist target, which is how Dave and I died.
output.missing_information:
1. Whether I had been swapped: the user of a redirected action is told nothing, so my last Juror result was wrong in a way I couldn't detect.
2. A per-player table of stated votes against announced totals. I rebuilt this by hand in the notepad every Day, and it used most of the 425 words.
3. The ledger cut off Bob's final claim with "[truncated]" exactly where he changed his stated nomination vote, which was the key fact of that trial.
4. How many Yakuza and Neutrals the setup had. "2 to 4 Yakuza, 0 to 3 Neutrals" is a wide range in a 13-player game, and it made any endgame arithmetic guesswork. The Village only learned at the end that no Yakuza had died.
output.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. Use my last result: the N3 Juror check arrived the night I died, so it never reached my will or anyone else. As an investigator I'd have liked results from the death night to be appended to the will.
2. Do anything useful on Night 1: the Juror has no votes to compare, and Day 2 had only one nomination and one trial, so the N2 check was nearly empty too.
3. Compare more than one pair per night, or one player against the stated votes of several. One pair per night is too slow when two or more players die each night.

output.bugs_or_oddities:
1. The end-of-game "Night 3 actions" list is inconsistent about swapped targets. It shows my Juror action as "target Judy; second target Olivia", but I submitted Judy + Erin, and my own night history and result text both say Erin. It also shows all three Yakuza Katana votes as "attacks Erin" when the chat shows they voted Olivia, and Alice's result reads "Your Katana attack on Olivia succeeded". The actions list seems to show post-swap landing targets while the results show chosen targets; it should say which, or show both.
