output.suggestions:
1. Balance: this hand-picked setup gave the Yakuza two kills a night (Katana plus Ritualist), a swap and a doubled ballot. The Village had no protector, no killer and no alignment checker. A Jester with a fake Cartographer claim then cost the Village two hangs and triggered a revenge kill that chained into the Cardinal's curse. Include at least one Medic or Sheriff, or avoid pairing a Ritualist with mostly open-claim investigative roles.
2. Vote-audit roles are weak when the Yakuza simply vote with the majority and state their votes honestly. The Juror, the two Scrutineer claims and my checks all just confirmed stated votes. Consider letting the Juror see which specific votes matched, or check a pair on nominations that failed.
3. Tell the user of an action when a swap redirected it, at least for astral checks, or state clearly in each role's text that they won't be told.
4. Append results from the night a player dies to their revealed will, perhaps only for investigative roles, so that killing an investigator doesn't erase the last result as well.
5. Add an automatic stated-vote table to the ledger (claimed vote per player per nomination and trial, beside the totals), and never truncate claim text there.
6. End the game, or at least announce it, when the Yakuza hold an unbreakable majority, as on Day 4 here; that Day was a formality.

output.reason: Post-game questionnaire: reporting concrete rule ambiguities, log inconsistencies and balance observations from my game as Bloodhound.

reasoning:
I'm drafting feedback as Dave the Bloodhound, noting that the attack-counting rule was ambiguous between per-player and aggregate totals, and that my result treated it as an aggregate when the phrasing could be read either way.

Also unclear was whether a Bloodhound's token-track action counts as a visit, since the role text doesn't specify this and my notes show uncertainty there. The scent token accounting across night two was a little confusing in message order (spending one on Bob, gaining one from the Philanthropist) but ultimately consistent, and since I died I never got to share my N2 result showing zero attacks among Bob, Erin, and Frank.

I notice I passed on submitting any scent action during night one, which I could have used. There are also a few ledger inconsistencies worth flagging — Bob being listed both as "role hidden" and revealed as Jester, and the Katana attack that was reported as landing on Olivia but actually hit Erin per rule 23 — plus the Jester's revenge targeting Olivia when it seemingly should have redirected to Erin under that same rule.

The Philanthropist's gift from Mallory also appears to be a bug: it targeted Olivia but the swap rule should have redirected it to Erin, yet the log shows Olivia receiving and discarding the token rather than Erin. That's inconsistent with how the swap mechanic is supposed to work.

The results name Olivia while the action list says "attacks Erin" post-swap, another inconsistent display. I'm also noting my own misstep—publicly announcing a scent token made me the Ritualist's target, though lessons aren't tracked here. There's also a truncated Jester claim history in the ledger worth flagging.

I want to suggest clarifying the Bloodhound's "combined total" wording and whether the scent track counts as a visit, since per-player counts would be more useful.    - The Yakuza chat and their summary say the Katana vote was on Olivia, and the result says "Your Katana attack on Olivia succeeded". The action list says "Katana vote: Alice holds, attacks Erin".
   - Carol's action shows "second target Olivia", but her result names Erin.
   - Showing "chose X, landed on Y" for each swapped action would make this readable.

2. **I was still shown a "current last will" and asked for a notepad after the game ended and I was dead.** Harmless, but odd.

3. **Day 4 trial total.** Five votes from four voters was announced with the "a role manipulated the count" note. That worked as documented.

4. **Setup balance.** The Village had no protector, no Sheriff, Tracker or Coroner, and no role reveal on death. It faced three Yakuza (Ritualist, Smuggler, Ballot Stuffer) plus a Jester, a Magpie and a Cardinal. It hanged only Village or Neutral players and had no realistic way to confirm anyone.
answers.suggestions:
1. Show the claim length limit and warn before truncating.

2. Show the player's own votes for the Day beside the claim and message box.

3. In the post-game log, give both the chosen and the landed target for every swapped action.

4. State in R23 whether random automatic attacks (Jester's revenge, Cardinal's curse) and astral vote-history checks (Juror, Scrutineer, Auditor) are moved by a swap, with one example.

5. Let dead players, or at least a Jester who has already won, watch the rest of the game. Failing that, send a one-line note saying whom the revenge hit.

6. For hand-picked setups, give the Village at least one role that can confirm something (Coroner, Chronicler or Sheriff) when no roles flip on death. Otherwise a single fake investigative claim, like my fake Cartographer, can't be disproved before the hang.

7. Consider giving a Jester a small night-time prompt, even just a will update, so the role isn't idle half the game.

answers.suggestions:
1. Balance: this hand-picked setup gave the Yakuza two kills a night (Katana plus Ritualist), a swap and a doubled ballot. The Village had no protector, no killer and no alignment checker. A Jester with a fake Cartographer claim then cost the Village two hangs and triggered a revenge kill that chained into the Cardinal's curse. Include at least one Medic or Sheriff, or avoid pairing a Ritualist with mostly open-claim investigative roles.
2. Vote-audit roles are weak when the Yakuza simply vote with the majority and state their votes honestly. The Juror, the two Scrutineer claims and my checks all just confirmed stated votes. Consider letting the Juror see which specific votes matched, or check a pair on nominations that failed.
3. Tell the user of an action when a swap redirected it, at least for astral checks, or state clearly in each role's text that they won't be told.
4. Append results from the night a player dies to their revealed will, perhaps only for investigative roles, so that killing an investigator doesn't erase the last result as well.
5. Add an automatic stated-vote table to the ledger (claimed vote per player per nomination and trial, beside the totals), and never truncate claim text there.
6. End the game, or at least announce it, when the Yakuza hold an unbreakable majority, as on Day 4 here; that Day was a formality.
7. Raise the notepad cap for larger games; it should scale with player count.

2. R23 swaps applied to "historical" astral checks (Juror, Scrutineer) are unintuitive. A swap on N3 changed whose past votes Carol's Juror check read, while the result still named the player she chose. The rule covers it, but an example for vote-history roles would help.
3. The Roleplayer rule gives every liar a free rebuttal: any real Lookout, Accountant or Oracle who contradicts a fake claim "may be an unknowing Roleplayer". The rules never say how likely a Roleplayer is, so I had no basis to weigh "two Roleplayers" against "one fake Cartographer", and I weighed it wrong.
4. The Yakuza count of "2 to 4" is very wide for parity maths. On Day 4 I could not tell whether the game was still winnable (it was not: 3 Yakuza of 4 alive).
answers.missing_information:
1. Any confirmation of a dead player's role or alignment. With no reveal on death and no Coroner in the setup, the Heidi hang told us nothing, and the Jester's fake Cartographer claim could not be tested before it cost a second day.
2. The number of Yakuza alive or in the setup. I had to reason "only winnable if Heidi was Yakuza" with no way to check.
3. My own budget history was hard to plan around. I reached the decisive Day 4 trial with almost nothing left, and I did not have a clear picture of how much a failed nomination would leave me for a defence.
4. The ledger truncated Bob's last claim ("[truncated]") exactly where he changed his stated nomination vote, which was the key fact of that trial.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. Get any information from my role when the Yakuza simply stated their real votes. Both my results only confirmed public statements, so the Scrutineer gave nothing for the whole game (and nothing at all on N1).
2. Choose all three players, or scrutinize nomination votes, to aim at a specific suspect.
3. Prove my role against a counter-claim. Frank (Smuggler) claimed Scrutineer before me and described it correctly from the rules, and there was no mechanical way to separate us. Quoting the moderator's exact wording was my only attempt, and it cannot work against anyone who has read the rules.
4. Do something useful once a nomination failed on the last Day. With 3 of 4 votes held by Yakuza there was no action left that mattered.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. The end-of-game "Night 3 actions" list seems to show post-swap targets (Alice "attacks Erin", Carol "second target Olivia" but her result names Erin, Mallory "target Olivia"), while the Yakuza night summary and Alice's result show the chosen target ("attack on Olivia succeeded"). The two views of the same night disagree, and nothing says which is the submitted choice and which is where it landed.
2. Night 1 events are tagged "[Day 1 night]" although the rules say there is no Day 1. It is consistent, but it reads oddly beside "Night 1 begins".
3. The game ran a full Day 4 with 3 Yakuza among 4 living players. That follows R1, but the Day was a formality: Yakuza controlled every nomination and trial.
4. Bob's claim in the ledger was cut off with "[truncated]".
5. Not a bug, but the hand-picked setup felt lopsided: 3 Yakuza including a Ritualist (two extra kills), a Jester and a Cardinal, against a Village with no protector, no killer and no role-reveal role. The Village lost 9 players without removing a single Yakuza, and the Jester win plus revenge plus Cardinal curse killed three Good players in one night.
answers.suggestions:
1. State in the Scrutineer text that names are listed alphabetically, and whether the accused and same-Day hanged players can be drawn.
2. Make the Scrutineer less dependent on Yakuza lying about votes: let it pick two of the three, or also report nomination votes, or give it something on N1.
3. Give the Village at least one way to confirm a dead player's role in setups this size (a Coroner or Chronicler), or reveal alignment on hanging. Otherwise a fake result claim costs a full Day to disprove.
4. Tell players the rough odds of a Roleplayer being present, or limit it to one per game, so "you might be a Roleplayer" is not an all-purpose rebuttal.
5. Narrow the published Yakuza range, or publish the exact count, so players can do parity maths.
6. In the final reveal, show both the submitted target and the landed target for swapped actions.
7. Do not truncate claims in the ledger; if space is needed, cut the "earlier" history first.
8. Consider ending the game, or announcing that the outcome is decided, once Yakuza hold a strict majority of votes and no Village kill role is alive.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. Ritualist tokens on a wrong guess: the role says "spending 1 token for a Standard Attack or 2 for a Divine Attack. If right, the Attack is dealt. If wrong, [you are announced]". It never says whether a wrong guess still spends the token(s), or whether a role-blocked Ritualist is spared the public announcement. I assumed the token is spent and a block cancels everything (R9), but had to guess.
2. Swaps and moderator-driven attacks: R23 says "every action that night aimed at one of them" is moved. It is unclear whether that covers the Jester's revenge and the Cardinal's curse, which are random draws, not anyone's choice. On N3 we swapped Olivia and Erin, and Olivia died to the Jester's revenge. I can't tell whether Olivia was drawn or Erin was drawn and redirected.
3. Exact wording and layout of private results is undocumented. Ivan tried to verify Frank's fake Scrutineer claim by quoting the moderator's line word for word ("names alphabetical, not target first"). A faker cannot know that format from the rules, so it becomes an out-of-rules tell. Either document each role's result format or say explicitly that format knowledge is fair game.
4. The "[Claim]" ledger entry is not described in the rules (only mentioned in passing under Puppeteer). I worked it out from the turn prompts.
5. R1's end condition: the game continued on Day 4 with 3 Yakuza and 1 Villager alive. That is consistent with "all living players belong to one faction", but I was unsure at first whether a locked majority ends the game.
answers.missing_information:
1. What a real Oracle result looks like. I was faking Oracle and had no template for the wording, so I kept my fake results vague ("guessed X = Y, wrong").
2. No way to tell teammates by day that my cover log had changed. I had agreed "Niaj = Vanilla, wrong" in night chat, but Niaj's will said Vanilla, so I had to switch to "Sheriff, wrong" on the spot. This is by design, but a reminder in the Day prompt of what cover each teammate agreed would help.
3. Vote bookkeeping was manageable only because of the notepad. A fixed "your own votes so far" section in each prompt would free notepad space.
4. The ledger truncated Bob's last claim ("[truncated]"), right where he changed his stated nomination vote. That was the detail that mattered.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. End Day 4 early. With 3 Yakuza against 1 Villager and nominations needing 3 Yes, the outcome was fixed, but we still had to stage a fake result, a nomination and a full trial.
2. See both the target the team voted for and the player the Katana landed on, when a teammate's swap redirected it. Alice's result said "attack on Olivia succeeded" while Erin died. That is correct under R23, but a Yakuza-side note such as "redirected by your team's swap" would avoid confusion.
Otherwise none.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Post-game "Night 3 actions" appears to show targets after the swap, not as submitted. It lists the Katana vote as "Alice holds, attacks Erin", but all three of us submitted Olivia; my own night history and the Yakuza summary say Olivia. Carol's Juror entry shows "second target Olivia" while her result names "Judy and Erin". The 1-of-2 trial figure matches Olivia's votes, so the swap itself resolved correctly, but the log mixes chosen and landed targets without labelling which is which.
2. Four deaths in one night (Katana, Ritualist, Jester's revenge, Cardinal's curse) took the game from 8 alive to 4, with 3 of those Yakuza. This is by the rules, but it decided the game instantly.

The Yakuza had a Ritualist with two extra kills. A Jester's invented Cartographer results hanged the real Lookout on Day 2, and a Cardinal punished the Village further. We were never in danger.

answers.suggestions:
1. State explicitly whether a wrong Ritualist guess spends tokens, and how role-blocks interact with the public announcement.
2. State in R23 whether swaps redirect random moderator-driven attacks (Jester and Executioner revenge, Cardinal's curse).
3. In post-game and night-history logs, show both "chosen" and "landed on" for any action a swap redirected.
4. End the game automatically once one faction has an unbreakable voting majority and no living role can change that, or at least once the Village cannot mathematically pass a nomination.
5. Add a short canonical result template to each investigative role's text. Fakers and real claimants are then on equal footing, and wording quizzes stop being a meta-tell.
6. Don't truncate claims in the ledger when a claim changes a previously stated vote; flag the changed part instead.
7. For hand-picked setups, give the Village at least one protective or blocking role when the Yakuza include a Ritualist. Otherwise any exact-role claim that isn't on the Roleplayer list is a free kill, as Bloodhound and Juror were here.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. Philanthropist: the rules don't say whether a gift can push a recipient above their starting token count, whether a token handed over tonight can be spent tonight, or whether the gift still lands if the recipient dies that night. Dave's log suggests it is added after his own spend, but I had to guess while playing.
2. Philanthropist and swaps (R23): my N3 gift to Erin was moved to Olivia and I was never told. That is by the rules, but for a role with no feedback at all it means my only proof (the recipient confirming) can silently point at the wrong person. The role text could note this.

4. R1's win check: on Day 4 the Yakuza were 3 of 4 living players and controlled every vote, yet the game ran on. That is correct by the rules, but a line saying there is no early "majority" win would help.
answers.missing_information:
1. As Philanthropist I get no result line at all, not even "your token was delivered". I had to infer I wasn't role-blocked from the absence of a block notice.
2. There is no public or private indication of which claimed roles hold tokens, so choosing a recipient was guesswork from the rules text.
3. Bob's claim in the ledger ended in "[truncated]", which cut off his stated trial vote. That was the very thing being argued about on Day 3.
4. Stated votes against totals had to be tracked by hand in the notepad. A per-trial table of stated votes next to the announced totals in the ledger would save a lot of notepad space.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. Prove my role. A Philanthropist can only be confirmed by a living, honest, token-holding recipient. I gave to Dave, who died the same night, and the Jester then used "unconfirmable by design" against me.
2. Ask a private follow-up during a trial without paying for it from the same small budget as the public statement I needed to make.
3. Keep a fuller vote log. The 425-word notepad was about 80% full by Day 3 of a 13-player game.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. The post-game "Night 3 actions" list is inconsistent with the other records. It shows my target as Olivia and Alice's Katana as attacking Erin (the landed targets), while my own night history says Erin and the Yakuza summary says Olivia (the chosen targets). Nothing marks which is which.
2. The ledger lists "Bob (role hidden, executed by hanging)" and on the next line "Bob (Jester) won". This is harmless but contradictory.
3. Four Village-side deaths in one night (Katana, Ritualist, Jester's revenge, Cardinal's curse) took the game from 8 alive to 4 with all 3 Yakuza untouched. The revenge hitting the Cardinal chained into a second Divine kill on a Good player, so one mis-hang cost three Villagers. This follows the rules but is extremely swingy.

answers.suggestions:
1. Give the Philanthropist a minimal receipt each night ("your token was handed over", without saying whether it was useful), or tell them when a swap moved the gift.
2. In post-game logs, show both targets for swapped actions, e.g. "chose Erin, landed on Olivia (swap)".
3. Never truncate the vote part of a ledger claim. Truncate the free text first, or put votes in their own field.
4. Add an auto-maintained table of stated votes against totals to the ledger.
5. Consider stopping the Cardinal's curse from triggering off Jester's or Executioner's revenge, or capping non-Yakuza chain deaths per night, so one bad hang can't remove three Villagers.
6. With 13 players, a hand-picked setup of 3 strong Yakuza (Ritualist, Smuggler, Ballot Stuffer), a Jester, a Magpie and a Cardinal against a Village with no protective or killing role and mostly vote-reading investigators felt close to unwinnable. A Medic or one alignment-checking role would balance it.
7. Raise the notepad cap for games with 12 or more players.

answers.confusing_rules:
Three points in the Magpie text and R19 were unclear to me:
1. "A second steal from the same player takes nothing" could mean no token is removed at all, or that a token is removed but doesn't count toward the win. I assumed the first.
2. R19 says how the Sheriff reads Jester, Executioner, Serial Killer and Arsonist, but not Magpie, Bounty Hunter or Vulture. I assumed Not Evil, but had to guess when planning a cover claim.
3. Stealing from a Roleplayer who believes they hold tokens (e.g. a fake Seer) is not covered. R19 says they are "seen as having 0 tokens" for the Accountant, but not whether a Magpie steal fails the same way.

The note "Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens" sits next to a setup described as hand-picked, so I couldn't tell whether that guarantee applied here.
answers.missing_information:
On Night 1 I had nothing to go on for the Magpie's only decision. There are no claims yet, and no hint of how many token roles are in the game, so the steal was a blind 1-in-12 pick; it hit a Vanilla Villager.

After dying on Night 1 I received nothing until the full reveal, which is fine, but it meant my whole game was one uninformed choice and a will.

The tips have no Magpie section, e.g. which claims tend to hold tokens, or whether to skip Night 1 and wait for Day 2 claims.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
I wanted to hold my first steal until I had heard Day 2 claims without losing a night, but Night 1 comes before any discussion, so the choice was guess blind or waste the night.

I would also have liked to see my Night 1 steal result before the death notice in a way I could act on, such as updating my will. Both arrived together, and the will stayed as written before Night 1.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. The end-of-game "Night 3 actions" list appears to show where actions landed after the swap, not what players chose, and doesn't say so. The Yakuza chat agreed on target Olivia, and Alice's private summary says "chose to attack Olivia", but the list says "Katana vote: Alice holds, attacks Erin". Carol's entry reads "second target Olivia" while her result names "Judy and Erin". It took me a while to see these were consistent under R23.
2. The Juror's vote-history comparison was redirected by the Smuggler's swap. That follows R23 as written, but it is strange for an astral check of past votes, and it silently gives the Juror the wrong player's data.
3. Bob's claim in the public ledger ends in "[truncated]", cutting off his stated trial vote.
4. My notepad still said "N1 tried Erin (result pending)" at game end, because I never got a turn after the result arrived.
answers.suggestions:
1. Give the Magpie some survivability or early information. Basic Defense does nothing against the Standard Katana, and a win needs at least three nights. Options: Standard Defense on Night 1 only, or a start-of-game count of how many players hold tokens.
2. In the end-of-game action log, show both "chose X" and "landed on Y (swapped)" for any redirected action.
3. Say in R19 how every Neutral role reads to the Sheriff.
4. State in the Magpie text what happens on a repeat steal and on a steal from a Roleplayer.
5. Add a short Magpie section to the tips.
6. Don't truncate ledger claims mid-field; drop the oldest "earlier:" history first.
7. Let players who die at night make one final notepad update after seeing that night's results, so post-game reflection has accurate notes.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. R23 (swaps) versus automatic effects. It is unclear whether a Jester's revenge or a Cardinal's curse counts as an "action aimed at" a player and so gets moved by a swap. On Night 3 I was told "any action aimed at you landed on them instead", yet I died to Jester's revenge the same night. I could not tell whether the revenge drew Erin and was swapped onto me, or drew me and ignored the swap.
2. R23 versus notifications to the target. The rule says results name the player the user chose, but it does not say who receives target-side messages such as "a Philanthropist handed you a token" (see bugs).
3. Cardinal. The text does not say whether the curse can be stopped by any Defense (it is Divine, so presumably not), or whether the victim's death announcement always names "Cardinal's curse". It did, which publicly confirms that a Cardinal died and that the victim was Good. That is worth stating in the role text, because it decides whether the Cardinal should claim.
4. "Outsider" Cardinal gives no guidance on whether hiding the role is expected. I claimed Vanilla, and the fake claim then became part of other players' case against me.
answers.missing_information:
1. No role is ever revealed on death, so with 13 players the Village never learned whether the Heidi hang was right. Every later day was built on an unresolved guess, and I had no result of my own to anchor on.
2. The setup range (2 to 4 Yakuza, 0 to 3 Neutrals) is wide. I could not do parity maths, such as "how many mislynches can we afford", with any confidence.
3. Keeping every player's stated vote for each nomination and trial in a 425-word notepad was tight by Day 3. I had to drop older detail to fit the vote log.
4. In the ledger, Bob's final claim was cut off with "[truncated]" exactly where his corrected vote statement was. That was the part that mattered.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. I had no way to act on my role at all. Cardinal has no night action, no day ability and no information, so my whole game was chat plus votes. I would have liked some lever, even a one-time one, such as privately proving my role to one player.
2. I wanted to tell one trusted player I was the Cardinal without everyone seeing that a PM was sent and without a possible Wiretap reading it. The only safe channel was my will, which is only read after the damage is done.
3. I wanted to see my own vote history in the ledger automatically instead of logging it by hand in the notepad.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Probable swap bug. On Night 3 Frank swapped Olivia and Erin, and Mallory (Philanthropist) targeted Olivia. By R23 the gift should have landed on Erin, but I (Olivia) received "A Philanthropist handed you a token, but you threw it away". Either the gift was not moved by the swap, or the notification went to the chosen target instead of the real recipient. Both of us were tokenless, so the effect was hidden, but with a token role it would matter.
2. In the same night I was told every action aimed at me landed on someone else, yet I was killed by Jester's revenge. That may be correct (revenge drawn on Erin, then swapped), but nothing in the log lets anyone verify it.
3. The end-of-game reveal is inconsistent. The Night 3 action list says "Katana vote: Alice holds, attacks Erin" for all three Yakuza, while their chat, the Yakuza summaries and Alice's result all say the target chosen was Olivia. The action list seems to show the post-swap target while the results show the chosen one.
4. This post-game questionnaire still showed me a live-style prompt (ledger, notepad, will and "every response has a reason field" instructions), although I had been dead since Night 3.
answers.suggestions:
1. Make R23 explicit about which effects a swap moves: revenge, the Cardinal's curse, Philanthropist gifts and Magpie steals. Also say who gets the target-side notification.
2. Give the Cardinal some agency or information. As written it is a pure liability with nothing to do for the whole game. Alternatively, say plainly in the role text that the curse's cause of death is announced, so the player can weigh claiming.
3. Have the program add each player's own nomination and trial votes to their private history. That frees the notepad for reads.
4. Raise the notepad cap, or exempt an auto-generated vote table from it, in 13-player games.
5. Do not truncate claim text in the ledger mid-sentence. If it must be cut, drop the oldest claim history first.
6. Consider revealing the alignment (not the role) of hanged players, or including a guaranteed Coroner in larger hand-picked setups. In this game the Village hanged a Lookout, a Jester and a Scrutineer and never received one confirmed fact.
7. In the end-of-game log, show both the chosen target and the swapped landing target for each action.

answers.confusing_rules:
I answer from the game record; these are the points where a rule had to be interpreted.

1. **Swaps and non-visit actions (R23).** "Every action aimed at one of them" was applied to Carol's Juror check on Night 3. Her result was labelled "Judy and Erin: 1 of 2 trial votes", but that is the Judy+Olivia figure; the true Judy+Erin figure is 0 of 2. This follows the rule's letter, but a one-night swap falsifying a lookup of past vote records is surprising. The rule should say outright whether Astral or record-based actions (Juror, Scrutineer, Oracle, Coroner) are swapped.

2. **Swaps and posthumous attacks.** R23 doesn't say whether a Jester's or Executioner's revenge, or a Cardinal's curse, is an "action aimed at" a player. On Night 3 the revenge killed Olivia, who was swapped with Erin. The record doesn't show whether it was drawn on Erin and moved, or drawn on Olivia and left alone. Frank assumed in Yakuza chat that it would be moved.

3. **R23 "results don't show the swap" versus public death causes.** Alice was told "Your Katana attack on Olivia succeeded" while the public announcement said Erin died to the Katana and Olivia to Jester's revenge. Had Olivia survived, an attacker who didn't know about the swap would see "succeeded" on a living target. The rule should say what the attacker is told in that case.

4. **Bloodhound wording.** "You learn their names and how many Attacks they have made in total" can mean a count per player or one combined number. The result delivered was a combined number ("together they have made 0 attacks").

5. **Philanthropist timing.** The Magpie rule states when a steal lands relative to the night's token use; the Philanthropist rule doesn't. Dave spent a scent token and received one on Night 2, and was told "You now have 2" and then "2 scent tokens left", which doesn't make the order clear.

6. **Cardinal's curse ordering.** I read "after all of that night's other actions and attacks" as also coming after the Jester's revenge that killed the Cardinal. The rule could name revenge attacks explicitly.

7. **R1 end condition at a locked majority.** Day 4 began with 3 Yakuza and 1 Villager. Nothing Ivan could do would change the outcome, since a nomination needed 3 Yes votes, but the rules required the Day to be played.
answers.missing_information:
1. **Individual votes.** The record shows only totals. I could check the Juror and Scrutineer results (Carol's Night 2 and Night 3, Ivan's Night 2 and Night 3) only by rebuilding votes from what players said publicly. A moderator needs a ledger of each player's vote on every nomination and trial, including the vote as counted after a Fixer or Ballot Stuffer.

2. **Random draws.** Nothing records the original draw for the Jester's revenge, the Cardinal's curse, the Bloodhound's two random slots or the Scrutineer's added players. That made the swap question above impossible to settle afterwards.

3. **Chosen versus landed targets on a swap night.** The Night 3 action list shows only one of the two, with no label saying which.

4. **Seat order.** The circle is never listed; I inferred it from the Day 2 speaking order. It matters for the Surveyor and Diviner and for checking turn order.

5. **Speaking budgets.** No balances or prices appear in the record. I can't tell whether a short message or a silent player was a choice or a budget limit. The same goes for the cut-off in Bob's Day 3 claim entry, which ends in "[truncated]".

6. **Token state per player per night.** It had to be pieced together from separate result lines.

7. **End-of-game summary.** It lists winners but not the reason (Yakuza the only faction left after Ivan's hanging) and not the outcome for the Magpie, Niaj.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. **Flag an unwinnable position.** At the start of Day 4 the Yakuza held 3 of 4 votes and the Katana. There was no way to end the game or announce that it was decided, so a full nomination and trial were run for nothing.

2. **Annotate a result as swap-affected in the moderator-only record.** For example, "Carol chose Erin, landed on Olivia" would make a later audit possible.

3. **Tell a player why their claim entry was cut off, or what the length limit is.** Bob's entry was silently truncated in the middle of the sentence correcting his stated vote, which was the point everyone was judging him on.

4. **Deliver a result to a player who dies that night.** Grace's audit showing Bob with 0 tokens and Dave's scent on Bob were both produced and then lost, because wills are locked before the night. This is by design, but it meant the Village's only two hard checks on Bob never surfaced.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. **Night 3 action list contradicts the results.** The revealed list says all three Yakuza voted "Alice holds, attacks Erin". The Yakuza chat locked the vote on Olivia, the summary says "chose to attack Olivia", and Alice was told "Your Katana attack on Olivia succeeded". The list seems to show where the action landed after the swap, while results show the chosen name. Carol's entry is the same: it says "second target Olivia" but her result names "Judy and Erin". Mallory's "target Olivia" is therefore ambiguous. The list should show both, clearly labelled.

2. **Carol's Night 3 Juror result was factually false because of the swap.** It follows R23, but it is worth confirming this is intended for an Astral check on historical votes.

3. **Result wording varies from night to night for the same role.** The Ritualist got "Your guess tonight was right… You have 1 ritual token left" on Night 2 and "Your guess was right… You spent 1 ritual token; 0 ritual tokens left" on Night 3. Alice's ballot-token result and Katana result were merged into one message on Night 3.

4. **Wording became a way to prove a role.** On Day 4 Ivan quoted the moderator's private line word for word and pointed out that names are listed alphabetically, so a faker couldn't know the format. Any drift in templates feeds or breaks this.

5. **The Yakuza night summary repeats the Smuggler's free-text note** ("Spend 1 swap token: swap Olivia and Erin for the night.") after already saying the same thing.

6. **Bob's claim entry was truncated mid-sentence** ("[truncated]") with no notice to anyone.

7. **Four deaths on Night 3, not a bug.** Katana, Ritualist, Jester's revenge and Cardinal's curse took the game from 8 alive to 4 and from contested to decided, with no Day in between.

8. **No private messages were sent all game.** Every Day's discussion also happened almost entirely inside trials. On Day 3 there were two open-floor messages before the nomination, and on Day 4 one.
answers.suggestions:
**Rules**

1. State in R23 whether swaps redirect Astral or record-based checks and posthumous attacks (Jester or Executioner revenge, Cardinal's curse). Also state what an attacker is told when a swapped attack kills someone else.

2. Reword the Bloodhound to "the combined number of Attacks the three have made". Give the Philanthropist a timing line like the Magpie's.

3. Print the exact result templates for each role in the rules, or forbid quoting moderator text. Otherwise knowing the wording is an out-of-game way to authenticate a claim.

4. Consider ending the game, or offering a concession, when one faction holds an unbreakable voting majority and the night kill.

5. Rethink the incentives around trials. Trial turns are cheaper and a hanging ends the Day at once, so players nominate early to talk cheaply ("a trial gives everyone cheap turns"), and nobody can discuss a reveal such as "Bob was the Jester". A short discussion round after an execution, or less of a trial discount, would help.

**Setup balance**

6. This hand-picked setup gave the Village no protector and no alignment check. It had three vote-record roles, which are of little use when everyone states votes honestly. It also had a Jester and a Cardinal, against a Ritualist, a Smuggler and a Ballot Stuffer. No Yakuza died. One Medic or Sheriff, or dropping one of the two harmful roles, would make it a contest.

7. The Magpie died on Night 1 after hitting a player with no tokens. It gets no information on who holds tokens and needs three different victims. Consider giving it a hint.

**Moderator tooling**

8. Add a per-player vote ledger and a log of every random draw.

9. Show chosen and landed targets separately on swap nights.

10. Show the seat order, plus token and speaking-budget state for each player in each phase.

11. Give an explicit win reason and per-player outcome at the end.

12. Send a notice when a claim entry is truncated, and publish the length limit.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Never vote Guilty on anyone who might be a Jester or an Executioner's target. The revenge hits a random Guilty voter, and if it hits you your curse kills a second Good player. Vote Innocent, say why, and let others carry the hang.

Don't hang on one unverified result that was held back and then aimed at the claimant's own accuser. If two visiting claims corroborate each other (e.g. an audit matching the target's token count) against one counter, believe the pair. Two unknowing Roleplayers at once is far less likely than one liar.

If the accused offers a cheap one-night test and the accuser waves it off, take the test instead of hanging on Day 2. A real investigator welcomes verification. A refused test plus a Yes vote on their own nomination points to a Jester, so leave them alive and unhanged.

Night kills on investigators don't show who the Yakuza are protecting. They kill strong info roles because those roles threaten them in general. Don't conclude that the player those investigators were about to test must be Yakuza.

When two players claim the same role, don't assume the second claimant copied the first. The fake often claims early with a role whose results only repeat publicly stated votes. Test both early by asking for details only the real role would know, such as the exact wording of the moderator's result line, while there are still enough Good votes to act.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged. Eager self-nominators and easily disproved lone claims are often Jesters. If you must hang one, aim for a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent, since the revenge hits a random Guilty voter.
tips_feedback.why: The tip was right and the Village ignored it. Bob voted Yes on himself with a provably false claim, yet we hanged him 8-1. The revenge killed me (Cardinal) and my curse killed Mallory. Yakuza Judy followed the tip, voted Innocent and stayed out of the revenge pool.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers on purpose... While the Katana is still killing, avoid spending hangs on Neutrals that never block your win (Jester, Executioner, Bounty Hunter, Magpie).
tips_feedback.why: The tip was correct and ignoring it lost the game. We spent the Day 3 hang on a Jester while all three Yakuza were alive, and went from 9 alive to 4 with 3 Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a player is shown Yakuza by a mechanical result, look next at who defended them, urged delay or PM'd them.
tips_feedback.why: Bob was never mechanically shown Yakuza, but players applied this anyway. Several wills and Ivan pointed at Bob's early 'defenders' (Mallory, me, Alice). Two of the three were Good, so the suspicion landed on villagers while Frank and Judy went unexamined.

You must survive the nights before your hang, since Basic Defense doesn't stop the Katana. Being the town's obvious next hang protects you: Yakuza leave a prime suspect alive and kill the people testing you instead.

When a claimant holds back a result and then aims it at the player who just accused them, and refuses offered tests of the claim, don't hang the accused on it that Day. Run the test overnight first. When a town claimant posts a result you know is false (e.g. a map naming the wrong Katana visitor), they are a Jester or other Neutral, not a Villager. Let town hang them, keep one of your team on a stated Innocent citing Jester risk to dodge the revenge pool and earn credit, and kill the players who contradicted the liar so their deaths 'confirm' the next mislynch.

Before the day you expect parity, count votes in night chat for each possible outcome (3v2, 3v3, 2v3) and script who posts, who nominates and how each votes. Stack every extra kill source the same night (Katana + ritual + swap past a possible Medic + doubled ballot); going from 9 alive to 4 in one night left the town no chance to regroup.

A count or map that 'comes before any visitor claims' is not proof of honesty: a Jester or Evil can invent it and call every contradicting visitor a Roleplayer. If a claimant refuses a cheap verification test and two visiting roles contradict them, wait one night for the test instead of hanging the contradictor.

tips_feedback.why: For the Village: they treated Bob's uncorroborated map as the 'mechanical fit' and hanged the real Lookout 9-3 on Day 2. A single unverified claimant's result is not corroboration, and the tip doesn't make that clear enough.

lessons.tip: "Too reckless a lie to be fake" is not evidence. A Jester wants a reckless, checkable lie. When one unverified info claim (a count or map) contradicts two visiting claimants, do not hang the people it accuses on timing alone. If a one-night test exists (a secret gift or visit the claimant must report), vote Innocent, run it, and hang with proof the next day.

In a 13-player game with a Katana plus a Ritualist, the Yakuza kill two a night, so the Village gets about two hangs in total. Do not spend the Day 2 hang "for vote records" or on a claim duel. After a mishang, check who rode the majority quietly: here all three Yakuza voted Yes and Guilty with the crowd, and the three Innocent voters were all Village.

An "Oracle" whose guesses are all "wrong" and never checkable is the natural Ritualist cover, because both use astral role guesses. Treat it as unverified. Be most wary when its first decisive result appears the moment its owner is nominated, and when it contradicts a role that is not on the Roleplayer list.

Gift early (Night 1) to someone likely to survive and able to confirm you publicly. Avoid the player who just announced a night action, since they are the obvious kill. A gift to someone who dies that night confirms nothing and looks invented. Remember a swap can redirect your gift without telling you.

Exact-role claims made on the first turn feed a Ritualist. Both Ritualist kills here were first-turn claims of roles off the Roleplayer list (Bloodhound, Juror). Once a Ritualist death appears, unclaimed players should stay vague or claim a Roleplayer-list role. Protectors should sit on the remaining hard claims.

A result that nobody else can check and that 'reveals' the killer only after its owner is accused is not a mechanical fit. If the claim only survives by calling two contradicting visitors Roleplayers, test it for a night (secret gift plus map, or a scent) before hanging anyone on it.

A player who votes Yes on their own nomination and tells easily disproved lies is probably a Jester. Leave them alive and ignore their results. Hanging them costs a hang, triggers a revenge kill and can chain into more deaths (a Cardinal, for example).

Do the parity math before each hang. With up to 4 Yakuza possible and two kills a night (Katana plus Ritualist), two wrong hangs lose the game by Day 4. If no kill victim could have been Yakuza, assume all of them are alive and hang only from the players nothing has cleared.

A Ritualist should spend tokens on roles claimed in the first turn that are not on the Roleplayer list (Bloodhound, Juror), one token each. Claim Oracle as cover: its guess is astral, and an invented 'X = role, WRONG' result can later discredit a real villager.

tips_feedback.why: Dave (Bloodhound) and Carol (Juror) claimed exact roles on Day 2 and the Ritualist killed both with correct one-token guesses on consecutive nights. The Village lost its two most checkable investigators.

lessons.tip: Never vote Guilty on anyone who might be a Jester or an Executioner's target. The revenge hits a random Guilty voter, and if it hits you your curse kills a second Good player. Vote Innocent, say why, and let others carry the hang.

Don't hang on one unverified result that was held back and then aimed at the claimant's own accuser. If two visiting claims corroborate each other (e.g. an audit matching the target's token count) against one counter, believe the pair. Two unknowing Roleplayers at once is far less likely than one liar.

If the accused offers a cheap one-night test and the accuser waves it off, take the test instead of hanging on Day 2. A real investigator welcomes verification. A refused test plus a Yes vote on their own nomination points to a Jester, so leave them alive and unhanged.

Night kills on investigators don't show who the Yakuza are protecting. They kill strong info roles because those roles threaten them in general. Don't conclude that the player those investigators were about to test must be Yakuza.

When two players claim the same role, don't assume the second claimant copied the first. The fake often claims early with a role whose results only repeat publicly stated votes. Test both early by asking for details only the real role would know, such as the exact wording of the moderator's result line, while there are still enough Good votes to act.

summary:
The Yakuza (Alice Ballot Stuffer, Frank Smuggler, Judy Ritualist) won without any of them being tried until Day 4, because the Village spent both of its real hangs on a claim fight a Jester started.

**Day 2.** Bob (Jester) claimed Cartographer with an invented "one visit" count. When the real Lookout (Heidi) and real Accountant (Grace) contradicted it, he produced a held-back "map" naming Heidi as the Katana holder. The Village accepted "he claimed before any visitor spoke" as proof and wrote off two independent contradicting claims as a double Roleplayer. It refused Heidi's cheap tests (Dave's scent, Mallory's token) and hanged her 9-3. The trial itself came from three vote-info claimants (the real Juror, the real Scrutineer and Frank's fake Scrutineer) asking for "a trial for vote records".

**Night 2.** The Yakuza killed the two investigators who could expose them. The Katana took Grace, whose audit would show a teammate's tokens. Judy's ritual took Dave, who had claimed Bloodhound by name and announced a scent. They deliberately left Bob alive as the Day 3 hang.

**Day 3.** The Village read the kills as "protecting Bob" and hanged him with 8 Guilty when 5 were needed, even though several players had named the Jester risk. Only Judy stayed Innocent.

**Night 3.** The night produced four deaths:
- The Katana killed Erin (via Frank's swap).
- The ritual killed Carol, who had claimed Juror by name.
- The Jester's revenge hit Olivia.
- Olivia was the Cardinal, so her curse killed Mallory.

**Day 4.** Nine alive had become four: Ivan against three Yakuza. They voted down his nomination of Judy and hanged him.

The decisive Village errors were treating an uncorroborated, late, accuser-aimed result as mechanical proof, hanging a likely Jester with every Good player in the revenge pool, and never examining the quiet claims (a Vanilla, an Oracle with only "wrong" guesses, a duplicate Scrutineer). The Yakuza won through discipline: unanimous Katana votes, no day PMs, truthfully stated votes, fake results built only from public information, and both ritual tokens spent on firm exact-role claims.

lessons.tip: A single-source result that is revealed late and names the claimant's own accuser is not a mechanical fit. "He claimed before the others spoke" shows boldness, not honesty, and bold falsifiable lies are what a Jester or bluffer wants. When two independent claimants contradict one counter, the story that needs two Roleplayers is the weaker one. If a cheap overnight test exists, take it instead of hanging.
lessons.evidence: Bob (Jester) posted a fake one-visit count, then a held-back map naming Heidi right after she named him her trial pick. Heidi (real Lookout) and Grace (real Accountant) both contradicted him and offered Dave's scent and Mallory's token test. The Village hanged Heidi 9-3 anyway.

lessons.tip: If the nominee might be a Jester, either don't hang them or hang with a bare majority. Investigators and any Cardinal should vote Innocent. Naming the Jester risk and then voting Guilty anyway is the worst of both. Ask who votes Yes on their own nomination and tells lies that are caught at once.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 Mallory and Judy named the Jester risk aloud and Olivia's will noted it, yet all five living villagers voted Guilty (8 Guilty, 5 needed). The revenge hit Olivia, a Cardinal, whose curse then killed Mallory. With the Katana and ritual kills the Village went from six players to one overnight.

lessons.tip: Read night kills as "who threatened the Yakuza", not "who threatened the current suspect". A suspect left alive while his testers die is often being kept as tomorrow's mislynch. Killed investigators were dangerous to the real killers, whose identities you don't know yet.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Night 2 plan read: "Bob is the natural D3 hang: leave him alive." They killed Grace (an audit would show 2 tokens on a Yakuza) and Dave (a scent would show Alice's attacks). Carol and Erin concluded "both kills protect Bob" and led his hang.

lessons.tip: A firm exact-role claim off the Roleplayer list, backed by an accurate result, is what a Ritualist waits for. Villagers should not name their exact role on Day 2 when they have no result or only a weak one, and should never announce tonight's action. Ritualists should hold tokens until such claims appear; one token is enough when there is no sign of a Medic.
lessons.evidence: Dave claimed Bloodhound with a low-value draw and said he would scent that night. Carol claimed Juror with no result at all. Judy skipped Night 1, then hit Dave = Bloodhound and Carol = Juror with one token each. Mallory and Olivia, who stayed vague at first, were never ritual targets.

lessons.tip: "A trial for vote records" is not a reason to execute anyone. Vote-audit roles catch nothing when the Yakuza vote with the majority and state their votes truthfully. Count the hangs you have left: with a Katana and a Ritualist killing two a night, the second hang may be your last real one, so it must go to a kill-faction candidate.
lessons.evidence: Carol, Ivan and Frank all asked for a Day 2 trial for records, and it turned into Heidi's execution. Every Juror and Scrutineer result afterwards just confirmed stated votes, because the Yakuza stated their real votes. At 9 alive on Day 3 the hang went to a Jester, and Day 4 opened with the Yakuza holding 3 of 4 votes.

lessons.tip: While a loud claim fight runs, audit the players coasting beside it: Vanilla claims, an Oracle with only "wrong" guesses, and any duplicated role. Settle duplicates the day they appear. Ask for something only the real role sees, such as the exact wording of the private result. Claim on your first turn so you are not the one who looks like the copier.
lessons.evidence: Alice (Vanilla), Judy (Oracle, three "wrong" guesses) and Frank (second Scrutineer) were never nominated before Day 4. Ivan, the real Scrutineer, opened vaguely and claimed after Frank, so he carried the "copied Frank" label all game. He raised the result-wording test only when three of the four living players were Yakuza.

lessons.tip: Let the Village's own fight do the hanging. Agree claims and fake results in night chat, build fakes only from publicly stated facts, state your real votes, and kill the investigators who can read you rather than the loud suspect. Split one vote off a possible Jester's trial and say why openly.
lessons.evidence: All three Yakuza cast identical Katana votes every night and sent no day PMs. Frank's fake Scrutineer results used only stated votes, so Ivan could not contradict them. Judy voted Innocent on Bob "to stay out of the revenge pool", which kept the team out of a 2-in-7 revenge risk for her and earned her credit when Bob flipped Jester.

lessons.tip: Claim an information role with bold, specific, falsifiable results and let night events break them. A proven liar who is not the killer gets hanged by a town that feels certain. Voting Yes on your own nomination and misstating it adds a "provable lie" that vote-trackers will seize on.
lessons.evidence: Bob's fake counts were broken by Grace's Katana death and Mallory's real gift. His stated "No" against 9 Yes of 9 became the lead argument for Carol, Erin, Frank, Ivan, Olivia and Alice. He was hanged 8-1 and won.

tips_feedback.why: It was correct and helped the one player who followed it: Judy voted Innocent on Bob and stayed out of the revenge pool. The villagers ignored it and voted 8 Guilty when 5 were needed. The revenge hit Olivia (Cardinal) and her curse killed Mallory.

issues.description: Night 3: the log cannot show whether Bob's Jester revenge was moved by Frank's Olivia/Erin swap. It prints only "[Revenge] Bob's Divine Attack hits Olivia", with no drawn-versus-landed target, and the moderator summary says revenge is "left to code". Both swapped players were in the Guilty-voter pool. R23 says every action aimed at a swapped player moves, but never says whether random post-night effects (Jester/Executioner revenge, Cardinal's curse) count. Frank assumed in Yakuza chat that they do. The "[Night check] Night 3: correct" line also appears before the revenge and the Cardinal's curse resolve, so the check seems not to cover them.

Swap-night labelling is inconsistent. In the Night 3 log the Katana vote reads "attacks Olivia", the resolution line reads "Katana: Alice holds it and attacks Erin", and Alice's result reads "Your Katana attack on Olivia succeeded". Each is defensible under R23, but nothing marks which is the chosen target and which is where it landed. Carol's post-game feedback reports the same problem in the end-of-game action list, which showed her Juror check as Judy + Olivia and the Katana votes as Erin, while her own history showed Judy + Erin and Olivia.

The Bloodhound text says you learn the three names "and how many Attacks they have made in total this game". That can be read as one number per player or one combined sum. The program gives a single sum ("together they have made 0 attacks"). A non-zero sum would not say which of the three attacked, which changes the role's strength, so the rule should say "combined" explicitly.

Night 2 Yakuza chat: Frank and Judy both treated Bob's fabricated Night 1 Cartographer count as verified. Frank: "Bob's N1 count (one visit) was actually correct, so he's probably a real Cartographer". Judy: "Bob's N1 count was true (one visit), so no Medic acted N1". Yakuza only know their own visits; Night 1 actually had four (Alice->Niaj, Grace->Heidi, Heidi->Ivan, Niaj->Erin). From this they wrongly concluded Grace was a Roleplayer and that no Medic existed, which fed Judy's choice of a 1-token ritual.

Day 3 trial: Bob's updated claim entry was cut off in the public ledger ("D3: Yes on my nomination (earlier \"No\" was a slip), [truncated]"). The claim field has a length limit that silently drops the end of the entry, here his stated trial vote. Players are apparently not warned of the limit, and they use the ledger to track stated votes.

Day 4: Ivan tried to prove his role by quoting the moderator's private result line verbatim and pointing out that the program lists names alphabetically ("Your scrutiny of Erin, Judy and Olivia: ..."), not target-first as Frank's fake results did. Fixed private-message wording and ordering thus work as an out-of-game way to tell real role-holders from fakes. It changed nothing here because every other voter was Yakuza, but it could decide a closer game on an interface detail.
